This pull request introduces a comprehensive agent specification for the new `source-planner` and `source-plan-executor`.

For local usage with the Copilot CLI:

- Start copilot CLI
- Select the `source-planner` agent using `/agent`
- Select the `claude-sonnet-4.5` or `claude-opus-4.5` model using `/model` (CLI does not use the model defined in the frontmatter)
- Run a prompt like `Please write a plan for an XXXX source and save it to file in my workspace`
- Once the plan is complete, review it and tweak it in the generated file
- Switch to the `gpt-5.2-codex` model using `/model`
- Switch to the `source-plan-executor` agent using `/agent`
- Run the prompt: `please implement the plan`

## Summary
Publish Aztec staking contract updates and documentation for v3.0.x readiness.

## Original Request
> Make a PR with the latest git commit with all the Aztec staking work

## Changes Made
- Migrate staking contracts to Aztec v3.0.x API and simplify architecture.
- Add integration + smoke tests for the 3-contract flow.
- Update staking progress + handoff documentation.

## Testing
- Not run in this session (not requested).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> Modernizes the liquid staking system for Aztec v3.0.x and consolidates to a focused 3-contract MVP with clearer interfaces and testing.
> 
> - **API/Architecture:** Migrates to v3.0.x (`external("public")`, `self.context.call_public_function`, etc.) and simplifies to `StakedAztecToken`, `LiquidStakingCore`, and `WithdrawalQueue`; removes legacy pool/managers/registry
> - **stAZTEC (ERC20):** Adds `approve/allowance/transfer_from`, maintains `total_aztec_backing`, and sets exchange rate as source of truth (`backing / supply`); `add_rewards` increases rate only
> - **Core flow:** `deposit(amount, nonce)` pulls AZTEC, mints stAZTEC via token; `request_withdrawal(st_amount, ts)` burns via token and enqueues withdrawal; queue handles claim after unbonding and supports funding
> - **Frontend views:** New getters (e.g., `balance_of_in_aztec`, `get_request`, `time_until_claimable`, protocol stats) to simplify integration
> - **Admin ops:** `collect_fees(nonce)` to treasury; `fund_withdrawal_queue(amount, nonce)`; pause/admin setters; min deposit enforced
> - **Tests & tooling:** Expand unit tests (+ERC20/rate invariants), add `integration-test.sh`, update `smoke-test.sh`; update guides (`NOIR_GUIDE.md` migration), progress, and handoff docs

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [gunicorn](https://pypi.org/project/gunicorn) from **20.1.0** to **24.0.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 23.0.0
   ```
   ===================

- minor docs fixes (:pr:`3217`, :pr:`3089`, :pr:`3167`)
- worker_class parameter accepts a class (:pr:`3079`)
- fix deadlock if request terminated during chunked parsing (:pr:`2688`)
- permit receiving Transfer-Encodings: compress, deflate, gzip (:pr:`3261`)
- permit Transfer-Encoding headers specifying multiple encodings. note: no parameters, still (:pr:`3261`)
- sdist generation now explicitly excludes sphinx build folder (:pr:`3257`)
- decode bytes-typed status (as can be passed by gevent) as utf-8 instead of raising `TypeError` (:pr:`2336`)
- raise correct Exception when encounting invalid chunked requests (:pr:`3258`)
- the SCRIPT_NAME and PATH_INFO headers, when received from allowed forwarders, are no longer restricted for containing an underscore (:pr:`3192`)
- include IPv6 loopback address ``[::1]`` in default for :ref:`forwarded-allow-ips` and :ref:`proxy-allow-ips` (:pr:`3192`)

** NOTE **

- The SCRIPT_NAME change mitigates a regression that appeared first in the 22.0.0 release
- Review your :ref:`forwarded-allow-ips` setting if you are still not seeing the SCRIPT_NAME transmitted
- Review your :ref:`forwarder-headers` setting if you are missing headers after upgrading from a version prior to 22.0.0

** Breaking changes **

- refuse requests where the uri field is empty (:pr:`3255`)
- refuse requests with invalid CR/LR/NUL in heade field values (:pr:`3253`)
- remove temporary ``--tolerate-dangerous-framing`` switch from 22.0 (:pr:`3260`)
- If any of the breaking changes affect you, be aware that now refused requests can post a security problem, especially so in setups involving request pipe-lining and/or proxies.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 22.0.0
   ```
   ===================

- use `utime` to notify workers liveness 
- migrate setup to pyproject.toml
- fix numerous security vulnerabilities in HTTP parser (closing some request smuggling vectors)
- parsing additional requests is no longer attempted past unsupported request framing
- on HTTP versions < 1.1 support for chunked transfer is refused (only used in exploits)
- requests conflicting configured or passed SCRIPT_NAME now produce a verbose error
- Trailer fields are no longer inspected for headers indicating secure scheme
- support Python 3.12

** Breaking changes **

- minimum version is Python 3.7
- the limitations on valid characters in the HTTP method have been bounded to Internet Standards
- requests specifying unsupported transfer coding (order) are refused by default (rare)
- HTTP methods are no longer casefolded by default (IANA method registry contains none affected)
- HTTP methods containing the number sign () are no longer accepted by default (rare)
- HTTP versions < 1.0 or >= 2.0 are no longer accepted by default (rare, only HTTP/1.1 is supported)
- HTTP versions consisting of multiple digits or containing a prefix/suffix are no longer accepted
- HTTP header field names Gunicorn cannot safely map to variables are silently dropped, as in other software
- HTTP headers with empty field name are refused by default (no legitimate use cases, used in exploits)
- requests with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length are refused by default (such a message might indicate an attempt to perform request smuggling)
- empty transfer codings are no longer permitted (reportedly seen with really old & broken proxies)


** SECURITY **

- fix CVE-2024-1135
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.2.0
   ```
   ===================

- fix thread worker: revert change considering connection as idle . 

*** NOTE ***

This is fixing the bad file description error.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.1.0
   ```
   ===================

- fix thread worker: fix socket removal from the queue
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.0.1
   ```
   ===================

- fix documentation build
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 21.0.0
   ```
   ===================

- support python 3.11
- fix gevent and eventlet workers
- fix threads support (gththread): improve performance and unblock requests
- SSL: now use SSLContext object
- HTTP parser: miscellaneous fixes
- remove unnecessary setuid calls
- fix testing
- improve logging
- miscellaneous fixes to core engine

*** RELEASE NOTE ***

We made this release major to start our new release cycle. More info will be provided on our discussion forum.

Changelog - 2024
================

author: silas-11
body:
## PR type

* [x] Bug Fix
* [ ] New Feature
* [ ] Document Updates
* [ ] More Models or Datasets Support

---

## PR information

### Background

When using **Accelerate FSDP2 on NPU backends**, model preparation may fail
during the FSDP2 initialization phase if the model parameters are not already
in `torch.float32`.

This issue is commonly observed in RLHF / GRPO training pipelines, where:

* `actor` and `ref` models are initialized in `bf16` / `fp16`
* `accelerator.prepare()` triggers `fsdp2_prepare_model`
* Accelerate internally performs a dtype cast to `fp32`

---

### Problem Description

On NPU backends, `accelerate.utils.fsdp_utils.fsdp2_prepare_model`
internally executes:

```python
model = model.to(torch.float32)
```

At this point, the model (or its parameters) may already be wrapped by **FSDP2**
and represented as **DTensor**.

This triggers the NPU operator:

```
npu._npu_dtype_cast
```

However, this operator **does not have a sharding strategy registered** in the
DTensor sharding propagation system, resulting in the following runtime error:

```text
NotImplementedError: Operator npu._npu_dtype_cast.default does not have a sharding strategy registered.
```

Full stack trace confirms the failure occurs during sharding propagation after
FSDP2 wrapping.

---

### Root Cause

* FSDP2 expects dtype casting to be completed **before sharding**
* On NPU, dtype cast operators do **not support DTensor sharding propagation**
* Performing `model.to(torch.float32)` **after** FSDP2 wrapping is therefore unsafe
* CUDA backends do not hit this issue due to different operator support

---

### Solution

This PR ensures that floating-point parameters are cast to `torch.float32`
**before entering the FSDP2 preparation stage** on NPU backends.

Specifically:

* Detect NPU backend via `Accelerator.device`
* Check whether model parameters are floating-point and not already `fp32`
* Perform an early dtype cast **before** FSDP2 sharding
* Avoid triggering any sharded dtype cast operators on NPU

Two internal entry points are patched:

1. `accelerate.utils.fsdp_utils.fsdp2_prepare_model`
2. `Accelerator._prepare_fsdp2`

The logic is guarded and **only active on NPU**, with no impact on CUDA or CPU
backends.

---

### Why this Fix Works

* The dtype cast happens on unsharded parameters
* No DTensor objects are involved during casting
* No NPU dtype-cast operators are executed on sharded tensors
* FSDP2 receives a model in a valid and expected state

This preserves the original Accelerate and FSDP2 behavior while avoiding an
unsupported execution path on NPU.

---

### Scope and Impact

* **Fixes**: NPU + Accelerate FSDP2 dtype cast crash
* **Affected workflows**: RLHF / GRPO / multi-model training (actor + ref)
* **Backends impacted**: NPU only
* **Behavior change on CUDA / CPU**: None
* **API changes**: None

---

## Experiment results

Verified on NPU backend:

* RLHF training with FSDP2 enabled
* `actor` and `ref` models initialized in `bf16`
* Training proceeds successfully without dtype cast errors


### Related Issue

Fixes #7871

body:
### Motivation
- Simplificar la navegación y reducir vistas duplicadas moviendo los listados dentro de las mismas páginas de formulario para centralizar flujo de trabajo.
- Eliminar vistas obsoletas de reportes y notificaciones automáticas para aligerar el menú y la interfaz.
- Mejorar la identidad visual y la experiencia de acceso en móviles aplicando el logo municipal configurable en todas las vistas de autenticación.
- Permitir que los usuarios suban una foto para usarla como avatar en la sesión y en la barra superior para una UX más clara.

### Description
- Eliminadas las vistas `reportes.php` y `notificaciones-automaticas.php` y limpiados los enlaces correspondientes en `partials/sidenav.php` para simplificar el menú.
- Añadida la columna `avatar_path` en `database/schema.sql` y la opción `logo_auth_height` para controlar el alto del logo en vistas de autenticación, más soporte en `municipalidad.php` y `app/bootstrap.php`.
- Implementada carga de avatar en `usuarios-crear.php` y `usuarios-editar.php` con almacenamiento en `uploads/avatars/`, validación de tipo y persistencia en la tabla `users` y en la sesión (`auth-2-sign-in.php`), además de mostrar el avatar en `partials/topbar.php` y `users-profile.php`.
- Movidos/insertados los listados dentro de sus formularios principales para centralizar gestión en `usuarios-crear.php`, `usuarios-editar.php`, `eventos-editar.php`, `autoridades-editar.php` y `roles-editar.php` y simplificados los dashboards `dashboard.php` / `dashboard-2.php` a shells más ligeros.
- Mejorada la marca en pantallas de acceso (`auth-2-sign-in.php`, `auth-sign-up.php`, `auth-2-reset-pass.php`, `login.php`, `recuperar-contrasena.php`) para usar `logo_auth_height` y textos en español.
- Añadida la tabla runtime y UI mejorada para matriz de permisos en `roles-permisos.php` con persistencia por `role_id` y un selector de roles.

### Testing
- Levantado servidor de desarrollo con `php -S 0.0.0.0:8000 -t /workspace/muni` y ejecutado un script Playwright que cargó `usuarios-crear.php` en viewport de escritorio y guardó la captura `artifacts/usuarios-crear-lista-avatar.png`, completándose con éxito.
- Comprobaciones manuales vía navegador local para verificar la carga de logo en vistas de auth, la subida de avatar y la renderización en la barra superior; no se ejecutaron pruebas unitarias automáticas.

------

author: itsmostafa
body:
## Summary
Refactors goralph to create unique implementation plan files per session in `.ralph/plans/` instead of using a single shared `.ralph/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` file. Each session now generates a timestamped plan file (e.g., `implementation_plan_20260122T143052.md`).

## Changes
- Replaced `ImplementationPlanFile` constant with `PlansDir` constant and `GeneratePlanPath()` function
- Added `PlanFile` field to `Config` struct for session-specific plan paths
- Updated `resetImplementationPlan()` and `buildPromptWithPlan()` to accept plan file path as parameter
- Added automatic creation of `.ralph/plans/` directory on startup
- Updated both `build` and `plan` commands to generate unique plan paths per session
- Updated documentation in CLAUDE.md and README.md

## Breaking Changes
None - `.ralph/` is already gitignored, so no migration of existing plans is needed.

## Test Plan
- [x] Run `task build` to verify compilation
- [ ] Run `goralph build -n 1` and verify:
  - New plan file is created in `.ralph/plans/`
  - Filename uses ISO 8601 compact format (YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS)
  - Plan file path is correctly referenced in agent prompt
- [ ] Verify no references to `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` remain in codebase

## Release Notes
Implementation plans are now session-scoped with unique timestamped files in `.ralph/plans/`. This prevents conflicts when running multiple sessions and provides better organization of plan history.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests pass locally (`task build`)
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Conventional commit format followed

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR fixes the Plane deployment in `modules/WebApp` by addressing configuration and database initialization issues.

1.  **Configuration**:
    *   Injects `WEB_URL` and `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` dynamically in `main.tf` using `local.predicted_service_url` to ensure the application works correctly behind the Cloud Run URL.
    *   Generates and injects a `SECRET_KEY` using Secret Manager, which is required for Plane's security features.

2.  **Database Initialization**:
    *   Updates the `db-init` job to use a more robust pattern (similar to Cyclos/Moodle).
    *   Explicitly sets the database owner to the application user (`ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO ...`).
    *   Grants `ALL ON SCHEMA public` to the application user, which is critical for PostgreSQL 15 compatibility where public schema permissions are restricted by default.

author: copilot
body:
Frontend was sending malformed job IDs to API causing 400/404 errors. Three issues: users copying "Job abc123" prefix from UI, truncated UUIDs (8 chars vs full), and no validation before API calls.

## Changes

### Core sanitization
- Added `sanitizeJobId()` - trims whitespace, strips "Job " prefix (case-insensitive), validates UUID format with regex
- Returns null with user-facing error for invalid/truncated IDs
- Applied to 9 functions: `analyzeCode()`, `runAgentPipeline()`, `runCodegen()`, `runTestgen()`, `runDocgen()`, `runDeploy()`, `runCritique()`, `prioritizeBugs()`, `startClarification()`

### Clipboard helpers
- Added `copyJobId()` using `navigator.clipboard` API with `execCommand` fallback
- Validates input before copying

### UI enhancement
- Updated `createJobCard()` to display clickable "Full ID: abc12345... (click to copy)" line
- Copies complete UUID to clipboard instead of truncated display value

## Example

Before:
```javascript
const jobId = document.getElementById('agent-job-id').value;
// User enters "Job 4bd1d352" → API call fails with 404
```

After:
```javascript
const jobIdInput = document.getElementById('agent-job-id').value;
const jobId = sanitizeJobId(jobIdInput);
if (!jobId) return; // Error: "Job ID '4bd1d352' appears to be truncated"
// "Job 4bd1d352-c80f-496a-bed7-4727e2a54145" → "4bd1d352-c80f-496a-bed7-4727e2a54145"
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Problem
> 
> The frontend has several job ID parsing issues causing 400/404 errors:
> 
> ### Issues Identified from Console Errors:
> 
> 1. **Job ID includes "Job " prefix**: The error `Job ID 'Job de56d37b' not found` shows users are entering "Job de56d37b" instead of just the UUID. The frontend should strip the "Job " prefix if present.
> 
> 2. **Truncated Job IDs**: API calls to `/api/generator/4bd1d352/codegen` show truncated UUIDs (should be full UUID like `4bd1d352-c80f-496a-bed7-4727e2a54145`). This happens when users copy/paste partial job IDs from the UI which displays `Job ${job.id.substring(0, 8)}`.
> 
> 3. **No UUID validation**: The frontend doesn't validate that job IDs are valid UUIDs before making API calls.
> 
> ### Console Errors:
> ```
> /api/generator/89b152b6-d8ae-4524-8c65-d2b9dfc02eda/clarify:1 Failed to load resource: 400
> /api/generator/4bd1d352/codegen:1 Failed to load resource: 404
> Job ID 'Job de56d37b' not found
> ```
> 
> ### Required Changes in `server/static/js/main.js`:
> 
> 1. **Add a `sanitizeJobId()` helper function** that:
>    - Trims whitespace
>    - Removes "Job " prefix (case-insensitive)
>    - Validates UUID format (with or without dashes)
>    - Returns `null` for invalid IDs with a user-friendly error
> 
> 2. **Apply sanitization to all functions that use job IDs**:
>    - `startClarification()` - line ~1586
>    - `runAgentPipeline()` - line ~774
>    - `runCodegen()` - line ~841
>    - `runTestgen()` - line ~873
>    - `runDocgen()` - line ~902
>    - `runDeploy()` - line ~931
>    - `runCritique()` - line ~960
>    - `analyzeCode()` - line ~411
>    - `viewJobDetails()` - line ~299
>    - `prioritizeBugs()` - line ~1244
>    - Any other function that reads from job ID input fields
> 
> 3. **Update `createJobCard()` function** (line ~237) to make the full job ID easily copyable:
>    - Add a "Copy ID" button or make the job ID clickable to copy full UUID
>    - Or show a tooltip with the full ID
> 
> ### Example Fix:
> 
> ```javascript
> /**
>  * Sanitize and validate a job ID input
>  * Handles common user input issues like "Job abc123" prefix or truncated IDs
>  * @param {string} input - Raw user input
>  * @returns {string|null} - Valid UUID or null if invalid
>  */
> function sanitizeJobId(input) {
>     if (!input) return null;
>     
>     // Trim whitespace
>     let jobId = input.trim();
>     
>     // Remove "Job " prefix (case-insensitive)
>     jobId = jobId.replace(/^job\s+/i, '');
>     
>     // UUID regex (with or without dashes)
>     const uuidRegex = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-?[0-9a-f]{4}-?[0-9a-f]{4}-?[0-9a-f]{4}-?[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
>     
>     if (!uuidRegex.test(jobId)) {
>         // Check if it's a truncated UUID (first 8 chars only)
>         if (/^[0-9a-f]{8}$/i.test(jobId)) {
>             showError(`Job ID '${jobId}' appears to be truncated. Please use the full job ID.`);
>         } else {
>             showError(`Invalid job ID format: '${input}'. Please enter a valid UUID.`);
>         }
>         return null;
>     }
>     
>     return jobId;
> }
> ```
> 
> ### Files to Modify:
> - `server/static/js/main.js`


</details>

author: veillette
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the CD48 codebase to improve maintainability and reduce duplication by extracting shared functionality into dedicated modules. Constants, utilities, protocols, and configuration handling are now centralized, making the code more modular and easier to maintain.

## Key Changes

### New Modules Created
- **`constants.py`**: Centralized hardware constants, timing parameters, and communication defaults previously scattered across `CD48` and `AsyncCD48` classes
- **`utils.py`**: Shared utility functions including device port detection, input validation, and voltage/DAC conversions
- **`protocols.py`**: Protocol definitions for type safety and interface contracts (TypedDicts for result types, runtime-checkable protocols for device interfaces)
- **`config.py`**: Unified configuration file loading and settings application logic extracted from `CD48.from_config()`

### Refactored Modules
- **`cd48.py`**: 
  - Removed duplicate constant definitions (now imported from `constants.py`)
  - Removed `_find_cd48()` method (now uses `find_cd48_port()` from `utils.py`)
  - Removed `_load_config_file()` and `_apply_config_settings()` (now use functions from `config.py`)
  - Removed exception definitions for `CD48ConfigError` and `CD48DeviceNotFoundError` (moved to respective modules)
  - Removed TypedDict definitions (moved to `protocols.py`)
  - Simplified imports and reduced file size by ~200 lines

- **`async_cd48.py`**:
  - Removed duplicate constant definitions
  - Removed `_find_cd48()` method
  - Updated imports to use new modules
  - Maintains backward compatibility by re-exporting constants as class attributes

- **`__init__.py`**: Updated imports to reflect new module structure

- **`experiments.py`**: Updated imports to use new module locations

### Backward Compatibility
- Class constants (e.g., `CD48.INIT_DELAY`, `AsyncCD48.NUM_CHANNELS`) are re-exported from the constants module, maintaining API compatibility
- All public exception classes remain accessible from their original import locations
- Result type definitions (TypedDicts) are accessible from both old and new import paths

### Benefits
- **Reduced duplication**: Constants and utilities defined once, used everywhere
- **Better organization**: Related functionality grouped into logical modules
- **Improved testability**: Utilities can be tested independently
- **Type safety**: Protocol definitions enable better IDE support and type checking
- **Easier maintenance**: Changes to shared logic only need to be made in one place

author: andygrove
body:
## Summary

Remove an unnecessary `String::clone()` in `maybe_concat_string_literal()`.

## Changes

```rust
// Before:
str.push_str(s.clone().as_str());

// After:
str.push_str(s);
```

Since `s` is already a `&String` (from the `ref s` pattern match), it can be passed directly to `push_str()` which accepts `&str`. The deref coercion handles the conversion automatically.

## Impact

This removes one heap allocation per concatenated string literal when parsing SQL with adjacent string literals like:

```sql
SELECT 'foo' 'bar'  -- Concatenates to 'foobar'
```

Small change but in the spirit of avoiding unnecessary allocations in the parser hot path.

body:
- `comfy/model_patcher.py`: added helper `_get_key_weight_meta` to read tensor `dtype` and `numel` metadata without touching materialized attributes.
- `comfy/model_patcher.py`: added helper `_get_key_weight_funcs` to obtain `set_*/convert_*` callables without reading the actual weight tensor.
- `comfy/model_patcher.py`: updated `low_vram_patch_estimate_vram` to use disk-weight metadata when `comfy.disk_weights.disk_weights_enabled()` is true.
- `comfy/model_patcher.py`: updated `ModelPatcher._load_list` (`_load_list`) to use metadata-based offload estimates when disk weights are enabled.
- `comfy/model_patcher.py`: updated `ModelPatcher.load` (`load`) to call `comfy.disk_weights.materialize_module_tree` for modules chosen to be materialized and to install `LowVramPatch` using the functions-only helper on disk-weights paths.
- `comfy/model_patcher.py`: updated `ModelPatcher.partially_unload` (`partially_unload`) to install `LowVramPatch` using the functions-only helper when disk weights are enabled.

### Motivation
- Ensure the `load` → `model_use_more_vram` → `partially_load` loading path never accesses a module's `weight` attribute before disk-weight lazy materialization, because some ops (e.g. `MixedPrecisionOps.Linear`) only create `weight` during `_load_from_state_dict` and thus lack the attribute until materialized.

### Description
- Added `_get_key_weight_meta` which resolves a module via `comfy.utils.get_attr`, checks `module._parameters`/`module._buffers`, and falls back to `comfy.disk_weights._state_dict_meta` when `comfy.disk_weights.disk_weights_enabled()` to obtain `(dtype, numel)` without materializing tensors.
- Added `_get_key_weight_funcs` which resolves `set_*/convert_*` callables via attribute lookup on the module without reading the tensor itself and used it to avoid premature `getattr(module, 'weight')` calls on disk-weight paths.
- Reworked `low_vram_patch_estimate_vram` and the `check_module_offload_mem` logic in `_load_list` to compute VRAM/offload estimates from metadata when disk weights are enabled and preserved original behavior when disabled.
- Replaced ad-hoc per-parameter streaming with `comfy.disk_weights.materialize_module_tree(m, placement_device)` when a module is chosen to be materialized, and replaced `state_dict()`-based fully-loaded detection with placement-accounting derived logic to correctly reflect lazy modules.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change set.

author: copilot
body:
The build failed attempting to pull `containai/full:latest` from Docker Hub (doesn't exist). The Dockerfile references a layered image that wasn't being built by the workflow.

## Changes

- **Workflow**: Build and push base → sdks → full layers sequentially before final image
  - Each layer pushed to GHCR with dynamic tags (`latest` for main, `pr-<number>` for PRs)
  - Separate cache scopes per layer for build efficiency
  - Fixed `IMAGE_NAME` to use `${{ github.repository }}`
  - Added OCI label build-args (VERSION, BUILD_DATE, VCS_REF) to all intermediate images
  - **PR build support**: Single-platform (amd64) builds for PRs with temporary tags
  - **Production builds**: Multi-platform (amd64, arm64) builds for main/tags with latest tags

- **Dockerfiles**: Reference GHCR images with parameterized build arguments
  - `Dockerfile.sdks`: `ARG BASE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/novotnyllc/containai/base:latest`
  - `Dockerfile.full`: `ARG SDKS_IMAGE=ghcr.io/novotnyllc/containai/sdks:latest`
  - `Dockerfile`: `ARG FULL_IMAGE=ghcr.io/novotnyllc/containai/full:latest`

## Build order
```yaml
base (Dockerfile.base)
  → sdks (Dockerfile.sdks, FROM base)
    → full (Dockerfile.full, FROM sdks)
      → containai (Dockerfile, FROM full)
```

## Build Strategy

**Pull Requests:**
- Builds amd64 only (faster validation)
- Pushes intermediate images with `pr-<number>` tag to GHCR
- Enables full build validation without multi-platform overhead

**Main Branch & Tags:**
- Builds amd64 + arm64 (full multi-platform support)
- Pushes intermediate images with `latest` tag to GHCR
- Final image gets additional tags (version, semver, sha)

All images now pushed to GHCR where workflow has authentication. No more Docker Hub pull failures or PR build failures.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #92

In dry-run mode with `--parallel`, the loop skips batch execution but never marks tasks as complete. Since `getNextTask()` returns tasks based on the `completed` flag in the YAML file, it keeps returning the same tasks, causing an infinite loop.

## Solution

Track processed task IDs in memory during dry-run mode (since we don't want to modify the source file in a dry run):

1. Added `dryRunProcessedIds` Set to track which tasks have been processed
2. Filter out already-processed tasks when fetching the next batch
3. Add tasks to the Set after each batch is "skipped"

## Testing

Before fix:
```
[INFO] Batch 1: 3 tasks in parallel
[INFO] (dry run) Skipping batch
[INFO] Batch 2: 3 tasks in parallel
...
[INFO] Batch 239919: 3 tasks in parallel
(runs forever)
```

After fix:
```
[INFO] Batch 1: 3 tasks in parallel
[INFO] (dry run) Skipping batch
...
[INFO] Batch 9: 1 tasks in parallel
[INFO] (dry run) Skipping batch

==================================================
[INFO] Summary:
  Completed: 0
  Failed:    0
  Duration:  147ms
==================================================
```

Tested against a 21-task YAML file with parallel groups - correctly processes 9 batches and terminates.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
**Context:** The `ServerInfo.from_tuple` method is used to deserialize server information received from other peers over the DHT. The previous implementation checked if the input tuple had *at least* two elements, which meant it would silently accept and ignore extra elements if a peer sent a malformed tuple (e.g., with 4 or more elements). This ambiguity could hide bugs, version incompatibilities, or other silent data corruption issues.

**Change:** This commit tightens the validation to explicitly check that the input tuple's length is either 2 or 3. If the length is anything else, it raises a `ValueError`. This makes the expected data structure invariant explicit. The corresponding unit test has been updated to verify this stricter check.

**Risk Reduced:** This change eliminates the risk of silently ignoring unexpected data in the `ServerInfo` structure. It makes the deserialization process stricter and more robust to malformed input from other peers, ensuring that any deviation from the expected format will fail fast and loudly, rather than leading to subtle, hard-to-debug issues.

**Verification:**
- Added a new unit test case in `tests/test_data_structures.py` to assert that a `ValueError` is raised for tuples with invalid lengths.
- Ran the test suite (`PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest tests/test_data_structures.py`) and confirmed that all tests pass.
- The change was reviewed and approved.

author: blaizzy
body:
## Summary

- Fix end-of-audio perturbation in Qwen3-TTS codec decoder by correcting the trim direction in `CausalTransposeConv1d` and `DecoderBlockUpsample`
- The causal transpose convolutions were incorrectly trimming excess samples from the left — they should trim from the right, matching reference implementations (Encodec, DAC, Mimi)

## Details

`ConvTranspose1d` produces `kernel_size - stride` extra samples. In a causal system, these artifacts appear at the end of the output (the tail of the last input's kernel). The previous code trimmed from the left, which kept these tail artifacts and caused an audible perturbation at the end of generated audio.

**Before:**
```python
x = x[..., self.left_pad : -self.right_pad]  # trims left
```

**After:**
```python
x = x[..., :-self.trim_right]  # trims right (correct)
```

## Test Plan

- Verified output shapes remain correct (`input_length * stride`) for all upsample rates (8, 5, 4, 3) and upsampling ratios (2, 2)
- Verified chunked decode produces correct lengths for both short and long sequences
- Listen to generated audio to confirm end-of-audio perturbation is gone

author: omarisadev
body:
Refactor: Implement Optimistic UI with React 19 Form Actions

# Description:
This PR refactors the chat messaging logic to fully leverage React 19's `useOptimistic` and Form Actions. This change addresses previous issues with message flickering, input lag, and race conditions when sending multiple messages rapidly.

# Key Changes:

* **Optimistic Updates:** Implemented `useOptimistic` to display messages immediately before the server response confirms them.
* **Form Actions:** Replaced the standard `onSubmit` handler with React `<form action>` to automatically manage transition lifecycles and pending states.
* **Uncontrolled Input:** Switched from controlled state (`value={message}`) to an uncontrolled input with `ref`. This allows for instant `form.reset()` execution, decoupling the input clearing from the React render cycle.
* **Robust Error Handling:** Implemented `requestAnimationFrame` rollback to reliably restore user input if a network request fails, avoiding race conditions with React's re-renders.

## Why:

* **Zero Latency:** The input field now clears instantly, and the message bubble appears immediately.
* **Correctness:** Prevents "stuck" sending states or duplicate bubbles when multiple messages are in flight simultaneously.

# How to Test:

1. **Rapid Fire:** Type and send multiple messages quickly. Verify that all appear instantly and transition to "sent" without duplicating.
2. **Network Failure:** Block the request in the Network tab or go offline. Send a message and verify that the input text is restored for retry.
3. **Latency Test:** Throttle the network to "Slow 3G" and observe that the input clears immediately while the message shows a "sending" state.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
💡 **What**: Optimized the PIL-based video generation path (used for GIF/WebP or when FFmpeg is missing) to use batched GPU-CPU transfers.
🎯 **Why**: Previously, the PIL path iterated over frames one by one, causing significant synchronization and kernel launch overhead for each frame.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces overhead by processing frames in chunks (default 20), theoretically improving performance for GIF/WebP generation from large tensor batches.
🔬 **Measurement**: Verified with `tests/test_pil_batch_optimization.py` which mocks the batch processing logic and ensures chunks are handled correctly. Confirmed `nodes/video_node.py` syntax is correct.

author: jakubhojsan
body:
## Summary

Patch release (2.0.1) that updates README documentation to reflect all v2.0 features and adds git tagging support to the version bump script.

**Changes:**
- Bumped version to 2.0.1 across package.json, Code.gs, and CHANGELOG.md
- Updated README with documentation for new v2.0 features:
  - Simplified `=EXA()` function
  - `systemPrompt` and `outputSchema` parameters for EXA_ANSWER
  - Domain/category filtering for EXA_SEARCH
  - Convert to Values feature
  - Rate limiting info
- Added `--tag` flag to bump-version.js script for automatic git commit and tagging

**New bump script usage:**
```bash
npm run bump patch          # Just update files
npm run bump patch --tag    # Update files + commit + create git tag
```

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify README function signatures match Code.gs** - The documented parameters for EXA_ANSWER and EXA_SEARCH should match the actual implementation
- [ ] **Test bump script with --tag flag** - Run `npm run bump patch --tag` on a test branch to verify it creates the commit and tag correctly

**Test plan:**
1. Review README examples against actual function behavior
2. Test `npm run bump patch` (without --tag) - should only update files
3. Test `npm run bump patch --tag` on a test branch - should commit and create tag

### Notes

The `--tag` flag commits and creates a git tag but does NOT push automatically - user must run `git push && git push --tags` manually. This is intentional to allow review before pushing.

author: kripken
body:
The External phase considers all externally-visible things and marks them
as such. That includes functions in a public table. The old code ran on each
item and processed it, which turns out to be very slow on Dart: Dart can
have massive tables with many repeated elements, so it is much faster to
first collect the function names in a set, then process those.

This makes `--gufa` on this large Dart testcase **7.7x** faster - not 7.7 percent,
but times: from 393 seconds to 51. (This is the same situation as in #8048,
again the huge table is not something we have handled well.)

author: anderskev
body:
## Summary

Enables configuring different LLM drivers and models for each agent (Architect, Developer, Reviewer, Evaluator, Brainstormer) within a profile. This replaces the single `driver`/`model` fields with an `agents` dict containing per-agent `AgentConfig` objects.

## Changes

### Added
- `AgentConfig` type with `driver`, `model`, and `options` fields
- `Profile.agents: dict[str, AgentConfig]` for per-agent configuration
- `Profile.get_agent_config(agent_name)` method to retrieve config
- Database schema migration warning for old databases
- New pipeline tests: `test_architect_node_config.py`, `test_developer_node_config.py`, `test_evaluation_node_config.py`, `test_reviewer_node_config.py`

### Changed
- All agents (Architect, Developer, Reviewer, Evaluator) now accept `AgentConfig` and create drivers internally
- Pipeline nodes use `profile.get_agent_config('agent_name')` instead of `DriverFactory`
- Database schema stores `agents` as JSON blob instead of separate columns
- ProfileRepository returns `Profile` objects (not `ProfileRecord`)
- Settings API endpoints return correct `is_active` status

### Removed
- `Profile.driver`, `Profile.model`, `Profile.validator_model` fields
- `ProfileRecord.driver`, `ProfileRecord.model` columns

## Motivation

Different agents have different needs. The Architect benefits from a reasoning-focused model (Claude), while the Developer might use a faster model for iteration. This change enables users to optimize cost and quality by choosing the right model for each role.

Closes #279.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (289 new/modified test cases)
- [x] Integration tests updated
- [x] All 1185 tests pass
- [x] mypy passes with no errors
- [x] ruff linting passes

### Manual Testing Steps

1. Delete `~/.amelia/amelia.db` (breaking schema change)
2. Start Amelia: `uv run amelia dev`
3. Create a profile with different agent configs via dashboard
4. Verify each agent uses its configured driver/model

## Breaking Changes

**Database schema change**: Old databases with `driver`/`model` columns are incompatible.

Migration:
```bash
rm ~/.amelia/amelia.db
uv run amelia dev  # Recreates with new schema
```

A warning is shown at startup if an old schema is detected.

## Related Issues

- Closes #279

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Tests pass locally
- [x] Linting passes
- [x] Documentation updated (CHANGELOG.md)

## Summary

Major refactoring of the geo file handling system with a unified GeoFormatRegistry:

- **GeoFormatRegistry**: Central dispatch for all geo format load/save operations with format auto-detection
- **Reorganized helpers**: Format-specific subdirectories (KML/, GeoJSON/, GPX/, SHP/, CSV/, WKT/, WKB/, GeoPackage/, OpenAir/)
- **New format support**: CSV points, WKT, WKB, GeoPackage, OpenAir airspace files
- **GeoUtilities**: Coordinate validation, Douglas-Peucker/Visvalingam-Whyatt simplification, UTM conversion, polygon operations
- **XsdValidator**: Schema-based validation for KML and GPX files
- **PlanImporter/PlanExporter**: Unified system with format-specific implementations

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed `filterMeters` parameter propagation in `loadFile()` to prevent double-filtering
- Fixed altitude validation test thresholds (50000 → 150000 to exceed kDefaultMaxAltitude)
- Added QSKIP for schema validation tests when resources unavailable

author: badrishc
body:
* Introduce `PostUpsertOperation`, `PostRMWOperation`, and `PostDeleteOperation` hooks to `ISessionFunctions` in TsavoriteKV, enabling actions after upsert, RMW, and delete but before record unlock. Critically, these hooks are invoked at a point where it is safe to pulse the TsavoriteKV epoch (no protected memory is accessed here/after this point).
* Add `IEpochAccessor` interface for epoch management by Post*Operation hooks.
* Refactor `TsavoriteLog.Enqueue` to accept an epoch accessor from caller (e.g., TsavoriteKV ISF callbacks in our case), ensuring we correctly suspend/resume the outer epoch during blocking log appends.
* Move AOF write logic in Garnet server to these post-operation hooks, using a `UserData` flag to defer logging until after the main operation (but before unlocking).
* Make `UpsertInfo`, `RMWInfo`, and `DeleteInfo` structs carry a `UserData` byte for application-specific operation flags.
* Update existing `ISessionFunctions` implementations with no-op post-operation hooks.
* Enums `UpsertAction`, `RMWAction`, and `DeleteAction` are now byte-sized to save a bit of stack space.

These changes ensure that if we block waiting for `AllocateBlock` during AOF logging in TsavoriteLog, we will not be holding the outer (TsavoriteKV-level) epoch, thereby preventing a epoch table full situation for other normal user operation (GET/SET) threads under very heavy workloads.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Adds macOS sleep detection to automatically stop listening when the system goes to sleep. This prevents the app from continuing to record/transcribe when the user closes their laptop lid or puts the system to sleep. The implementation uses `NSWorkspaceWillSleepNotification` and `NSWorkspaceDidWakeNotification` from macOS's NSWorkspace API to detect sleep/wake events. When sleep is detected, the frontend calls `stop()` to halt listening. Key changes: - New `sleep` feature in `crates/detect` with `SleepDetector` implementation - Proper cleanup via `Drop` impl that removes notification observers - Frontend handler in `listener.tsx` stops listening on sleep events - Updated TypeScript bindings with new `sleepStateChanged` event type ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify unsafe Objective-C interop in `sleep.rs`** - The `msg_send!` macros and notification observer registration/removal need careful review for memory safety - [ ] **Test on macOS by closing laptop lid** - This is the only way to verify the feature works. Confirm listening stops when system sleeps. - [ ] **Verify the app resumes correctly after wake** - The `SleepStateChanged { value: false }` event is emitted on wake but currently doesn't trigger any action (only sleep triggers stop) - [ ] **Check Linux build doesn't break** - The `sleep` feature is gated with `#[cfg(all(target_os = "macos", feature = "sleep"))]` but should verify CI passes **Recommended test plan:** 1. Start the app and begin listening/recording 2. Close laptop lid or trigger system sleep 3. Wake the system and verify listening has stopped 4. Verify no crashes or resource leaks after multiple sleep/wake cycles ### Notes - The implementation was optimized from the original diff to remove unnecessary threading complexity and add proper observer cleanup via `Drop` - Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7c0e8d2358254e61a702f88ebdcb0664 - Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/1b9ae9acc87349e393883ca54ed961c6 - Requested by @yujonglee, @ComputelessComputer ---

author: macattak
body:
## Summary

This PR completes the Epic 12B Tech Debt Resolution initiative, addressing 37 technical debt issues identified in the January 2026 comprehensive audit. The codebase quality has improved significantly through architectural refinements, complexity reduction, test improvements, and dependency hardening.

### Key Changes

- **Architecture Improvements**
  - Reduced `floe_core/__init__.py` public API from 76 to 15 essential symbols
  - Enforced explicit submodule imports for better maintainability
  - Split god modules (plugin_registry.py: 1230→350 lines)
  - Extracted OCI client helpers to focused modules

- **Complexity Reduction**
  - Reduced `map_pyiceberg_error()` cyclomatic complexity from CC 26 to CC 4
  - Reduced nesting depth to ≤4 across all functions
  - Applied Strategy Pattern for error handling dispatch

- **Dependency Hardening**
  - Pinned all critical dependencies with upper bounds (pydantic, kubernetes, pyiceberg, opentelemetry-*, pyarrow, oras, jinja2)
  - Verified 0 vulnerabilities via pip-audit

- **Test Quality**
  - Reduced test duplication using BasePluginDiscoveryTests pattern
  - Extracted shared fixtures to conftest.py
  - All 478 contract tests pass
  - 100% requirement traceability markers

- **Documentation**
  - Removed deprecated floe-cli package
  - Created follow-up issues for remaining god class decomposition

### Metrics

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Debt Score | 74/100 | 90/100 |
| `floe_core/__init__.py` exports | 76 | 15 |
| `map_pyiceberg_error()` CC | 26 | 4 |
| Skipped tests | 3 | 0 |
| Dependencies with upper bounds | 4 | 15 |

## Test Plan

- [x] All unit tests pass (`make test-unit`)
- [x] All contract tests pass (478 tests)
- [x] Type checking passes (`mypy --strict`)
- [x] Security scan passes (pip-audit, Aikido)
- [x] Imports work correctly (`python -c "from floe_core import ..."`)

## Linear Issues

### Completed Tasks
- FLO-1381 through FLO-1389: Dependency pinning (pydantic, kubernetes, pyiceberg, opentelemetry, pyarrow)
- FLO-1406 through FLO-1412: Complexity reduction (map_pyiceberg_error dispatch pattern)
- FLO-1425 through FLO-1431: Additional dependency bounds and audit
- FLO-1470 through FLO-1482: Polish phase (wildcard imports, performance hardening, documentation)

### Follow-up Issues Created
- [FLO-1483](https://linear.app/obsidianowl/issue/FLO-1483): Decompose OCIClient (1,335 lines) into focused modules
- [FLO-1484](https://linear.app/obsidianowl/issue/FLO-1484): Decompose PolicyEnforcer (811 lines) using Chain of Responsibility

body:
### Motivation
- Make Pool Royale pocket visuals and potted-ball framing match the Snooker Royal presentation.
- Ensure the aiming guide visually reaches short rails when no ball blocks the path, matching player expectations and reference photos.
- Prevent accidental cue-ball repositioning by requiring an explicit press-and-hold gesture for ball-in-hand dragging.

### Description
- Lowered the Pool Royale pocket net and strap heights to match Snooker Royal by adjusting `POCKET_NET_VERTICAL_LIFT` and `POCKET_STRAP_VERTICAL_LIFT` in `webapp/src/pages/Games/PoolRoyale.jsx`.
- Added `resolveRailIntersectionPoint`-based endpoint logic via a new `resolveAimLineEnd` helper and used it when building aim line endpoints so the aim guide extends to the rail intersection when no target ball is hit.
- Reworked the in-hand (ball-in-hand) indicator interaction to require a press-and-hold gesture (configurable `IN_HAND_HOLD_DELAY_MS`), implementing hold tracking, event snapshotting, pointer-capture handling, and cleanup (`inHandHoldTimerRef`, `inHandHoldEventRef`, `inHandHoldPointerRef`, etc.).
- Kept existing aim/swerve preview, cue follow, and remote-aim codepaths but replaced local `impact` usage with the `resolveAimLineEnd` result for both local and remote aim previews.

### Testing
- Started the web dev server with `npm --prefix webapp run dev` and confirmed Vite served the app (`VITE ready` log). (succeeded)
- Attempted an automated Playwright screenshot of `/games/poolroyale` to validate visual changes, but the screenshot run timed out while the page was rendering. (failed / timed out)
- No unit tests or linters were executed for this change set.

body:
This pull request introduces custom error handling for 404 and 500 errors in the Django backend, updates related URL configurations, and makes a minor change to AWS S3 settings. It also includes some updates to IDE configuration files.

**Error handling improvements:**
* Added custom handler functions `handler404` and `handler500` in `core/views.py` to render user-friendly error pages (`404.html` and `500.html`).
* Enabled these custom error handlers in `backend/urls.py` by assigning them to `handler404` and `handler500`.

**Configuration changes:**
* Changed `AWS_QUERYSTRING_AUTH` to `True` in `production.py` to enable query string authentication for AWS S3 resources.

**IDE and project file updates:**
* Added references to new static images and error templates, and made minor formatting changes in `.idea/workspace.xml`. author: pmanko
body:
## M3: File-Based Import Adapter

Implements file-based analyzer result import with directory watching and CSV/TXT parsing.

### Completed Tasks (T043-T059)

**Setup:**
- ✅ Created branch from demo/madagascar
- ✅ Verified Apache Commons CSV dependency (already present)
- ✅ Created Liquibase changeset for file_import_configuration table

**Backend Implementation:**
- ✅ FileImportConfiguration entity with JSON column mappings
- ✅ FileImportConfigurationDAO and DAOImpl
- ✅ FileImportService interface and implementation (file processing, archival, error handling)
- ✅ FileAnalyzerReader for CSV parsing with Commons CSV
- ✅ FileImportWatchService with @Scheduled polling (60s interval)
- ✅ FileImportRestController with CRUD endpoints

**Tests:**
- ✅ Updated ORM validation test to include FileImportConfiguration
- ✅ Created FileImportServiceTest with proper mocking (T047)
- ✅ Created FileAnalyzerReaderTest for CSV parsing (T048)
- ✅ Created FileAnalyzerReaderIntegrationTest for SpringContext scenarios
- ✅ Created test CSV fixtures (quantstudio-results.csv, malformed-results.csv, file-import-sample.csv)

**Frontend:**
- ✅ FileImportConfiguration React component with Carbon Design System
- ✅ fileImportService.js API client
- ✅ Jest unit tests for FileImportConfiguration component
- ✅ i18n keys added (English and French)

**Remediation:**
- ✅ Fixed FileImportServiceTest mock setup for AnalyzerResultsDAO
- ✅ Implemented FileImportServiceImpl.processFile() using FileAnalyzerReader
- ✅ Integrated duplicate detection warnings in FileAnalyzerReader
- ✅ Fixed frontend test import paths

### Acceptance Criteria Status

- ✅ CSV rows mapped to results via configured column mappings
- ✅ Processed files moved to archive directory
- ✅ Malformed files moved to error directory with log entry
- ✅ Files detected within 60 seconds (via @Scheduled polling)
- ✅ Duplicate detection warns before creating new results (with logging)

---

## Testing & Validation Steps

### 1. Backend Unit Tests

```bash
# Run FileImportService tests
mvn test -Dtest=FileImportServiceTest

# Run FileAnalyzerReader unit tests (CSV parsing)
mvn test -Dtest=FileAnalyzerReaderTest

# Expected: All tests pass
```

### 2. Backend Integration Tests

```bash
# Run FileAnalyzerReader integration tests (requires SpringContext)
mvn test -Dtest=FileAnalyzerReaderIntegrationTest

# Expected: Tests pass with Spring context available
```

### 3. Frontend Unit Tests

```bash
cd frontend
npm test -- FileImportConfiguration.test.jsx

# Expected: Tests pass (some may need assertion updates)
```

### 4. Manual End-to-End Testing

#### 4.1 Create File Import Configuration

1. **Via REST API:**
   ```bash
   curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/rest/analyzer/file-import/configurations \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{
       "analyzerId": 1,
       "importDirectory": "/tmp/test-import",
       "archiveDirectory": "/tmp/test-archive",
       "errorDirectory": "/tmp/test-error",
       "filePattern": "*.csv",
       "delimiter": ",",
       "hasHeader": true,
       "active": true,
       "columnMappings": {
         "Sample_ID": "sampleId",
         "Test_Code": "testCode",
         "Result": "result"
       }
     }'
   ```

2. **Via Frontend UI:**
   - Navigate to Analyzer Configuration page
   - Click "Add File Import Configuration"
   - Fill in form fields (analyzer, directories, column mappings)
   - Save configuration

#### 4.2 Test File Processing

1. **Prepare test CSV file:**
   ```bash
   mkdir -p /tmp/test-import
   cat > /tmp/test-import/results.csv << EOF
   Sample_ID,Test_Code,Result
   12345-001,HB,12.5
   12345-002,WBC,7500
   EOF
   ```

2. **Wait for scheduled poll (60 seconds) or trigger manually:**
   - The FileImportWatchService polls every 60 seconds
   - Check logs for file processing activity
   - Verify file moved to archive directory: `ls /tmp/test-archive/`

3. **Verify results in database:**
   ```sql
   SELECT * FROM analyzer_results 
   WHERE accession_number IN ('12345-001', '12345-002')
   ORDER BY lastupdated DESC;
   ```

#### 4.3 Test Error Handling

1. **Create malformed CSV:**
   ```bash
   cat > /tmp/test-import/malformed.csv << EOF
   Sample_ID,Test_Code,Result
   invalid,data,here,extra,columns
   EOF
   ```

2. **Wait for processing:**
   - File should be moved to error directory: `ls /tmp/test-error/`
   - Check application logs for error messages

#### 4.4 Test Duplicate Detection

1. **Re-process same file:**
   ```bash
   cp /tmp/test-archive/results.csv /tmp/test-import/results-duplicate.csv
   ```

2. **Check logs for duplicate warnings:**
   - Look for: "Duplicate result detected (will still be inserted)"
   - Verify results still inserted but marked appropriately

#### 4.5 Test Configuration Management

1. **List all configurations:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/rest/analyzer/file-import/configurations
   ```

2. **Get configuration by analyzer:**
   ```bash
   curl http://localhost:8080/rest/analyzer/file-import/configurations/analyzer/1
   ```

3. **Update configuration:**
   ```bash
   curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/rest/analyzer/file-import/configurations/{id} \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{...}'
   ```

4. **Deactivate configuration:**
   - Set `active: false` to stop polling for that analyzer

### 5. Configuration Validation

- **Import directory:** Must exist and be readable
- **Archive directory:** Created automatically if missing
- **Error directory:** Created automatically if missing
- **Column mappings:** Must include at least sampleId mapping
- **File pattern:** Supports glob patterns (e.g., `*.csv`, `results_*.txt`)

### 6. Performance Testing

- **Polling interval:** Configurable via `file.import.poll.interval` (default: 60000ms)
- **Concurrent files:** Multiple files processed sequentially per configuration
- **Large files:** Test with files containing 1000+ rows

### 7. Database Validation

- **Liquibase migration:** Verify `file_import_configuration` table created
- **Foreign keys:** Verify analyzer_id references analyzer table
- **JSON column:** Verify column_mappings stored as JSONB (PostgreSQL)

---

## Related
- Part of Feature 011: Madagascar Analyzer Integration
- Depends on: None (parallel with M1, M2)
- User Story: US-4 (File-Based PCR Thermocycler Integration)

author: dlorenc
body:
## Summary

- Adds `MULTICLAUDE_TEST_MODE` check to daemon's `startAgentWithConfig` function
- When test mode is enabled, skips claude binary resolution and startup while still registering agents in state
- Adds comprehensive tests for the test mode functionality
- Fixes failing coverage check from PR #252 by reverting the problematic `skipIfTmuxCantCreateSessions` helper

## Context

PR #248 added new E2E tests for the configurable agents feature that use the daemon's `spawn_agent` handler. These tests fail in CI because they try to resolve and start the claude binary, which isn't available in the CI environment.

PR #252 attempted to fix this but introduced a `skipIfTmuxCantCreateSessions` helper that caused race conditions when creating/killing tmux sessions in CI, leading to the coverage check failing with:
```
--- FAIL: TestWakeLoopSkipsRecentlyNudgedAgents (0.05s)
    daemon_test.go:1268: Failed to create tmux session: tmux new-session failed for session mc-test-wake-skip: exit status 1
```

This PR keeps the test mode fix from #252 but reverts the tmux skip helper back to the simpler `IsTmuxAvailable()` check that works reliably on main.

## Test plan

- [x] Run the previously failing tests locally: `go test -v -run "TestWakeLoopSkipsRecentlyNudgedAgents" ./internal/daemon/...`
- [x] Run full coverage: `go test -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic ./internal/... ./pkg/...`
- [x] All tests pass with coverage

author: copilot
body:
The reported SSRF vulnerability in webhook URL validation does not exist in this repository. The issue references files (`src/utils/webhook.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/jobs.ts`) from a different codebase.

## No Changes Required

This is a Next.js cat food tracker application with no webhook functionality:
- No `src/` directory structure (uses Next.js App Router: `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`)
- No user-provided URLs being fetched
- Single external fetch uses hardcoded GitHub API endpoint (`/app/api/feedback/route.ts`)

## Repository Analysis

API routes present:
- `/api/auth` - Authentication (Better Auth)
- `/api/feedback` - GitHub issue creation (safe, hardcoded URL)
- `/api/foods` - Cat food CRUD operations
- `/api/meals` - Meal tracking CRUD operations

The described vulnerability appears intended for a Cloudflare Worker or similar service handling user-provided webhook URLs.

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>SECURITY: Missing Webhook URL Validation (SSRF Risk)</issue_title>
> <issue_description>## Vulnerability Description
> 
> The application accepts user-provided webhook URLs without proper validation, creating a potential Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.
> 
> ## Severity: **High**
> 
> ## Affected Files
> 
> * `src/utils/webhook.ts:126` - Webhook URL is used directly in fetch without validation
> * `src/index.ts:92-95` - User-provided webhook_url is accepted from request body
> * `src/jobs.ts:15,29` - webhook_url stored without validation
> 
> ## Security Risk
> 
> An attacker could provide malicious webhook URLs to:
> 
> 1. Scan internal network services (localhost, internal IPs like 169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata)
> 2. Probe internal infrastructure through the Cloudflare Worker
> 3. Bypass firewall restrictions to access internal services
> 4. Exfiltrate data to attacker-controlled servers
> 
> ## Code Snippet
> 
> ```typescript
> // src/utils/webhook.ts:126
> const response = await fetch(webhookUrl, {
>   method: "POST",
>   headers,
>   body,
> });
> ```
> 
> ## Recommended Fix
> 
> 1. Implement URL validation to block:
>    * Private IP ranges (10.x.x.x, 172.16-31.x.x, 192.168.x.x)
>    * Localhost (127.0.0.1, ::1)
>    * Cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254)
>    * Non-HTTPS URLs in production
> 2. Implement an allowlist of permitted domains if possible
> 3. Use DNS resolution validation to prevent DNS rebinding attacks
> 
> ```typescript
> function isValidWebhookUrl(url: string): boolean {
>   try {
>     const parsed = new URL(url);
>     // Only allow HTTPS in production
>     if (parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return false;
>     // Block common internal/metadata IPs
>     const blockedHosts = ['localhost', '127.0.0.1', '169.254.169.254', '::1'];
>     if (blockedHosts.includes(parsed.hostname)) return false;
>     // Block private IP ranges
>     if (isPrivateIP(parsed.hostname)) return false;
>     return true;
>   } catch {
>     return false;
>   }
> }
> ```</issue_description>
>

body:
Resolves #88

This adds support for enum-constrained positional arguments, similar to how enum flags work.

## Features
- `BaseEnumPositionalParameter` interface for type-safe enum positionals
- Runtime validation with typo suggestions using Damerau-Levenshtein distance
- Completion support for enum values
- Help text formatting showing `(value1|value2|value3)` format
- Support for optional, required, and default value scenarios

## Example
```typescript
positional: {
    kind: "enum",
    values: ["small", "medium", "large"] as const,
    parameter: {
        brief: "Size selection",
        placeholder: "size",
        parse: String,
    },
}
```

## Tests
- 18 comprehensive tests covering all scenarios
- Tests pass with 100% coverage

body:
Instead of using a cache Matrix, saving the results to that and then summing up in on of the dimensions and writing the sum to a matrix entry, this adds directly to the final matrix, decreasing the number of allocations needed. 

I've run the model two times, before and after, to be sure the raw results are exactly the same.

I've also use Chairmarks to do a naive benchmark, just to have an idea of the improvement. The following is for a single `run_model` call:
```
## Previously
9.890 s (5060673 allocs: 2.831 GiB, 6.76% gc time, without a warmup)

## Now
6.659 s (5060363 allocs: 2.819 GiB, 8.64% gc time, without a warmup)
```

author: mengwong
body:
## Summary

- Adds formal specification for the `UPON` keyword in L4
- Models external events as `MAY` actions by a distinguished `Environment` party
- Establishes connection to event calculus, situation calculus, and process algebras (CCS/CSP)
- Clarifies that UPON is orthogonal to the homoiconicity/first-class obligations feature

## Key Design Decision

External events like floods, market price changes, or time passing are modeled as:

```l4
PARTY Environment MAY FloodEvent
HENCE
  PARTY Insurer MUST pay Customer
```

The `UPON` keyword is syntactic sugar for this pattern:

```l4
UPON FloodEvent
PARTY Insurer MUST pay Customer
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Review specification for completeness and consistency
- [ ] Verify alignment with existing regulative rule documentation
- [ ] Confirm orthogonality claim with homoiconicity spec

Closes #490

author: arrthurr
body:
## Summary

Fixes the countdown toast looping 2x when auto check-in triggers.

**Root cause:** The `activeCountdownRef` was being cleared BEFORE the async `checkIn()`/`checkOut()` operation completed, creating a race condition:

1. Countdown finishes, ref is cleared immediately
2. Poll fires during the async operation  
3. Poll sees no active countdown (ref is null)
4. New countdown starts while check-in is still in progress

**Fix:** Move cleanup to `finally` block so `activeCountdownRef` stays set during the entire async operation, blocking duplicate countdowns.

## Changes

- `onConfirm` for check-in: Wrap in try/finally, cleanup after async completes
- `onConfirm` for check-out: Same pattern
- Explicitly set `activeCountdownRef.current = null` in finally block

## Test Plan

- [x] Typecheck passes
- [ ] Manual test on live site - verify single countdown toast
- [ ] Monitor console logs for duplicate "Auto check-in countdown started" entries

author: jshchssr1023
body:
## Summary
This PR consolidates Prisma client usage across the backend by replacing direct `PrismaClient` imports with a singleton instance from the centralized `db` service. Additionally, it upgrades password hashing from SHA-256 to bcrypt for improved security.

## Key Changes

- **Prisma Client Refactoring**: Replaced all direct `import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'` statements with imports from the centralized `./db` service, ensuring a single Prisma instance is used throughout the application
  - Updated files: `shoppingStatusJob.ts`, `activeAssignmentsService.ts`, `autoAllocationEngine.ts`, `masterPlanService.ts`, `multiYearPlanningService.ts`, `planProposalService.ts`, `shopAllocationValidator.ts`, `shoppingStatusService.ts`, `ssotIntegrityService.ts`, `express.d.ts`
  - Added type alias `type PrismaClient = typeof prisma` for type compatibility where needed

- **Password Hashing Security**: Upgraded from SHA-256 to bcrypt in `init-db.js`
  - Changed `crypto.createHash('sha256')` to `bcrypt.hashSync(password, 10)`
  - Ensures consistency with bcrypt validation in `auth.ts`

- **Rate Limiting Import**: Simplified `auth.ts` by importing `loginRateLimit` directly from middleware instead of creating it inline
  - Reduces code duplication and improves maintainability

- **Type Imports**: Updated Prisma type imports to use centralized `prismaTypes` where applicable (e.g., `shoppingStatusService.ts`, `ssotIntegrityService.ts`)

## Implementation Details

- The singleton Prisma instance pattern prevents multiple client instances and ensures consistent database connections
- Bcrypt with salt rounds of 10 provides industry-standard password security
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing code while improving architecture consistency

### Description

- Added an `ASIN一覧` load button and related small catalog initialization improvements to avoid empty-state confusion while ASIN data loads.

author: manoj-inturi
body:
🍳 RecipeJS – Functional Cooking Companion

A modern, interactive recipe web application built using vanilla JavaScript, functional programming principles, and clean UI design.

This project is built step-by-step across multiple parts to demonstrate real-world frontend development practices.

🚀 Live Features (So Far)
✅ Part 1 – Foundation

Semantic HTML structure

Responsive CSS layout with flexbox

Stylish recipe cards with hover effects

Dynamic rendering using JavaScript

Data-driven UI (recipes rendered from JS objects)

✅ Part 2 – Interactivity with Functional Programming

Filter recipes by:

Difficulty (Easy / Medium / Hard)

Quick recipes (under 30 minutes)

Sort recipes by:

Name (A–Z)

Cooking time (Fastest first)

Active button indicators

Pure functions for filtering and sorting

No mutation of original data

Clean separation of concerns (data vs UI)

🛠️ Tech Stack

HTML5 – Semantic markup

CSS3 – Flexbox, gradients, hover effects

JavaScript (ES6+)

Arrow functions

Template literals

map(), filter(), sort()

Spread operator

DOM manipulation

No frameworks. No libraries. Just clean JavaScript 💪

### [`v4.0.2`](https://redirect.github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/releases/tag/v4.0.2)

#### :warning: Noteworthy Changes

If your application code depends on a class from `jetty-ee11-servlets`, declare a dependency on it in your build configuration. [#​48677](https://redirect.github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/48677)

-   No TransactionAutoConfiguration with spring-boot-starter-kafka for Spring Boot 4 [#​48880](https://redirect.github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/48880)
-   Evaluation of bean conditions unnecessarily queries the bean factory for types that are not present [#​48840](https://redirect.github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/48840)

This pull request introduces a complete payment reminders system, including backend API endpoints, scheduled job logic, and supporting database schema changes. The system enables users to configure reminder settings, send manual or automated reminders for invoices, and track reminder history.

**Key changes:**

### Database schema additions

* Added new `PaymentReminder` and `ReminderSettings` models to the Prisma schema, with appropriate fields and relations to `User` and `Invoice` for tracking reminders and user-specific settings. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5b443964f4f3a611682db8f7e02177b0a8c632b2039e2bd5e4dd7347815c565cR23-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5b443964f4f3a611682db8f7e02177b0a8c632b2039e2bd5e4dd7347815c565cR71-R96)
* Created a migration to add the `PaymentReminder` and `ReminderSettings` tables, including foreign keys and indexes.

### API endpoints for payment reminders

* Implemented `GET` and `PUT` endpoints in `payment-reminders/settings/route.ts` for retrieving and updating user reminder settings, including authentication and upsert logic.
* Added a `GET` endpoint in `payment-reminders/history/route.ts` to fetch the reminder history for a specific invoice, with authentication and access control.
* Implemented a `POST` endpoint in `payment-reminders/send/route.ts` to allow users to send manual reminders for invoices, including rate limiting (one per 24h), email sending, and reminder tracking.

### Scheduled reminders job

* Added a scheduled job in `lib/jobs/payment-reminders.ts` to automatically send reminders based on user settings and invoice due dates, ensuring no duplicate reminders are sent for the same offset/type. Includes email sending and reminder logging.


#### Next Steps
Cron Job: You need to set up a Cron job (e.g., Vercel Cron) to call a new API endpoint that invokes 
sendScheduledReminders()
.
Note: I implemented the job function but not the cron trigger endpoint itself as per prompt requirements focusing on the logic/routes. You can add a simple route app/api/cron/reminders/route.ts that calls this function.


closes #29

#### 📝 Explanation and details


The optimized code achieves a **9% speedup** by replacing an expensive nested-loop word-matching algorithm with a hash-map-based lookup, dramatically reducing computational complexity.

## Key Optimizations

### 1. **Algorithmic Improvement: O(n²) → O(n) Word Matching**
The original code used nested loops that repeatedly scanned the masked OCR regions array for each word in each text section:
```python

```

The optimized version builds a **single index map upfront** using `defaultdict(deque)`:
```python
index_map: dict = defaultdict(deque)
for idx, txt in enumerate(texts):
    index_map[txt].append(idx)
```

Now word lookups are **O(1) hash lookups** instead of O(n) scans. This is particularly effective for the large-scale tests where it achieves **21-35% speedups** (e.g., `test_large_number_of_text_sections`: 21.7% faster, `test_grouping_with_large_ocr_text`: 27% faster).

### 2. **Avoiding Repeated Array Masking Overhead**
The original code created boolean masks and repeatedly indexed `ocr_regions.texts[mask]` and `indices[mask][i]` inside nested loops—each indexing operation creates new array views. The optimized version accesses `ocr_regions.texts` once and stores indices directly in the map, eliminating repeated numpy indexing overhead.

### 3. **Micro-optimizations in `merge_text_regions`**
- Changed `.astype(float)` to direct `float()` calls, avoiding unnecessary numpy dtype conversions
- Replaced list comprehension `[text for text in ...]` with generator expression `(t for t in ...)` in `str.join()`, reducing intermediate list allocation

## Performance Characteristics

**Best for:**
- **Large OCR datasets with many text sections** (20-35% speedup observed in tests with 100-300 regions)
- **Scenarios with duplicate words** where the deque preserves OCR order and prevents index reuse
- **Dense text grouping operations** where many words need matching

**Minimal impact for:**
- Single regions or very small inputs (~1-4% improvement)
- Cases without `group_by_ocr_text=True` (unaffected by the main optimization)

Based on `function_references`, this function is called from `supplement_layout_with_ocr_elements()` in a PDF/image OCR pipeline. Since OCR typically processes:
- Multi-page documents with hundreds of text regions
- Multiple passes for layout supplementation

The optimization **directly benefits hot-path OCR processing**, especially for document-heavy workloads where text grouping is enabled. The 9% average speedup compounds across multiple page processing operations.

The optimization maintains identical behavior by:
- Sorting `regions` to preserve OCR scan order (original used masked indices which were inherently ordered)

## Changes in this commit

### Fixed Infinite Loop Risk
- Removed `useCallback` wrapper that was included in useEffect dependencies
- Moved fetch logic directly into useEffect body
- Added `retryCount` state to trigger re-fetch on retry without callback reference changes
- useEffect now only depends on `characterId`, `navigate`, and `retryCount`

### Removed Unsafe Optional Chaining
- Removed `lastTurn?.` optional chaining in JSX since the check at line 85 ensures it's non-null
- Changed final render to explicitly check `loadingState === 'success' && lastTurn`
- TypeScript now correctly understands lastTurn is non-null in the success branch

### Improved Error Status Property Access
- Changed from `(err as { status?: number })?.status` to safer type checking
- Now uses: `err && typeof err === 'object' && 'status' in err ? (err as { status: number }).status : undefined`
- Prevents runtime errors if err is null, undefined, or not an object

body:
## Summary
- Added `pytest-rerunfailures` dependency for automatic test retries
- Configured E2E tests to retry up to 2 times with 1 second delay between attempts
- Added convenience script `test-e2e` for local testing with retries

## Changes

### `pyproject.toml`
- Added `pytest-rerunfailures` to dev dependencies
- Added new `test-e2e` script: `pytest -sv -m e2e --reruns=2 --reruns-delay=1`

### `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- Updated E2E test command to include `--reruns=2 --reruns-delay=1` flags
- Retries only apply to E2E tests (via `-m e2e` marker)

## Benefits
- Reduces false failures from transient issues in CI
- Tests fail only if all 3 attempts (1 original + 2 retries) fail
- 1 second delay between retries allows transient issues to resolve
- Marker-based configuration ensures retries only apply to E2E tests

## How It Works
When an E2E test fails:
1. **First run**: Test executes normally
2. **First retry**: Waits 1 second, then reruns (if failed)
3. **Second retry**: Waits 1 second, then reruns (if still failed)
4. **Final result**: Test marked as failed only after all 3 attempts fail

## Usage

**In CI** (automatic):
```bash
# E2E tests automatically retry on failure
```

**Locally**:
```bash
# Use new convenience script
pdm run test-e2e

# Or manually
pdm run pytest -m e2e --reruns=2 --reruns-delay=1
```

## Test Plan
- [x] Linting passes (`pdm run lint`)
- [x] Code follows existing patterns
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass
- [x] pytest-rerunfailures dependency installed successfully
- [ ] Verify retry behavior in CI on test failure

## Description

Updates Roslyn to 5.0.0-2.26070.104 to match the 10.0.1xx SDK. The new analyzer version enforces IDE0071 and IDE0031 more strictly, causing build failures with `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`.

## Changes

**eng/Versions.props**
- Bump `MicrosoftCodeAnalysisVersion_LatestVS`: `4.14.0` → `5.0.0-2.26070.104`

**.editorconfig** (global `[*.cs]` section)
- Add `dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0071.severity = silent` - Suppresses false positives for `ReadOnlySpan<char>.ToString()` in string interpolations (required for netstandard targets where ReadOnlySpan cannot be directly interpolated)
- Add `dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0031.severity = silent` - Suppresses null propagation suggestions

Setting `silent` severity preserves IDE hints while preventing build errors.

- `System.Security.Cryptography.MLDsaImplementation.Windows.cs`

author: pboling
body:
## Summary

Fixes the extension build detection logic to match Bundler's behavior by checking the `extensions` field in gemspec metadata rather than filesystem presence of `ext/` directories.

## Problem

The previous implementation had two flaws:

1. **Incorrectly skipped platform-specific gems**: Platform != "ruby" was treated as always precompiled, but platform-specific gems can still require building if they don't have precompiled binaries for that variant.

2. **Incorrectly detected build requirements**: Checked for `ext/` directory presence on filesystem, which led to false positives (gems with `ext/` containing docs/precompiled binaries but no actual build requirements).

## Solution

Changed `NeedsBuild()` to use the authoritative source of truth: the `extensions` field from gemspec metadata, matching Bundler's approach (`build_extensions if spec.extensions.any?`).

### Key Changes

- **`internal/extensions/detect.go`**: 
  - Changed signature: `NeedsBuild(gemDir, extensions []string, engine)` 
  - Uses `extensions` metadata as source of truth
  - Empty `extensions` → no build needed (even if `ext/` exists)
  - Non-empty `extensions` → build needed (unless already built)
  - Supports `nil` extensions for git/path gems (falls back to filesystem check)

- **Updated all call sites** to pass `gem.Extensions` from metadata

- **Updated tests** to focus on metadata-based behavior

- **Fixed `TestPrecompiledGemsDoNotNeedBuilding`** to create proper cached gem file

## Bundler Compatibility

This matches Bundler's logic from `rubygems_gem_installer.rb` line 33:

```ruby
build_extensions if spec.extensions.any?
```

The `extensions` field in the gemspec explicitly declares build requirements, making it the correct indicator regardless of platform or filesystem content.

## Testing

✅ **All 56 internal/extensions tests pass**

✅ **Build compiles successfully** (`go build -mod=mod`)

✅ **Fixed precompiled gems test** - properly creates cached gem file

✅ **Verified**: regular gems, git gems, path gems, and precompiled gems all handled correctly

## Files Changed

- `internal/extensions/detect.go` - Updated NeedsBuild() signature and logic
- `internal/extensions/detect_test.go` - Updated tests to focus on metadata
- `internal/runtime/install.go` - Updated call sites to pass gem.Extensions
- `cmd/ore/install.go` - Updated call sites to pass gem.Extensions  
- `cmd/ore/install_precompiled_test.go` - Fixed test to create cached gem file

author: baileyryanlee
body:
### Motivation
- The Freeze/Shatter sword strike frequently failed to impart reliable knockback because damage application could overwrite velocity, so knockback must be applied after damage and instrumented to diagnose overwrites.

### Description
- Added debug instrumentation with `[FuseDBG] ShatterKB pre`, `[FuseDBG] ShatterKB postDamage`, and `[FuseDBG] ShatterKB applied` logs and an MVP confirmation log `[FuseMVP] FreezeShatterKB` to observe victim motion before/after damage and after knockback.
- Ensure knockback is applied after `Actor_ApplyDamage` rather than before, so damage handlers cannot silently clear the velocity.
- Compute a `knockbackYaw` using the attacker position when available and fall back to `victim->yawTowardsPlayer + 0x8000`, then set velocity via `Math_SinS`/`Math_CosS`, set `speedXZ`, update `world.rot.y`/`shape.rot.y`, and clamp the vertical component with `std::max` using `kFreezeShatterKnockbackYBoost`.
- Removed the previous inline per-branch velocity assignment so all knockback is applied in a single, consistent post-damage code path.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run.

By allowing verified collection points to update the price-per-kg of unverified batches, I have unlocked new levels of flexibility and market responsiveness, ensuring that pricing can adapt to fluctuating market conditions without the hassle of batch recreation or cancellation.
