author: l0rinc
body:
This is an alternative to #34293, but aims to address the remaining logging inconsistencies more broadly.
It extends the example fixed there to every instance, restores the original separator behavior, applies it consistently via a single helper, and adds tests for `logips` (covering both current and new behavior).

### Problem
After #28521 centralized peer address logging into `CNode::LogIP()`, the original comma separator before `peeraddr=` was lost, resulting in inconsistent formatting across net (and recent private broadcast) logs.
Some lines also had double spaces, empty fields, or mismatched format specifiers.

### Fix
Introduces `CNode::LogPeer(bool)` which always emits `peer=<id>` and, when `-logips=1`, appends `, peeraddr=<addr>`. This eliminates hand-rolled separators and makes peer identification predictable.
Minor issues (double spaces, empty placeholders, format specifiers) are fixed along the way in separate commits.

### Reproducer
Run with `-debug=net -logips=1` and observe peer log lines now show `peer=<id>, peeraddr=<addr>` (comma-separated). The new assertion in `feature_logging.py` automates this check.

* Add handling for auth-based campaign visibility in frontend

The documentation covers embedded media security, testing plans, and JWT authentication setup for WordPress. The E2E test verifies that admin actions correctly interact with REST endpoints. These changes improve clarity for developers and QA, enforce secure media handling, and provide automated coverage for critical admin workflows.

## Type of change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] 🌟 New feature
- [ ] 🔨 Refactor
- [x] 📚 Documentation
- [ ] ⚡ Performance

## Description

Introduces Property-Based Testing (Fuzzing) using `fast-check` to validate the stability of the `convertOoxml` parser.

### Key Changes:
1.  **New Test:** `tests/fuzz/ooxml.fuzz.test.ts`.
2.  **Strategy:** Generates 1000 random, deeply nested, and malformed XML structures per run.
3.  **Assertion:** The parser MUST NOT throw an exception (crash). It must either return a result or handle the error gracefully.
4.  **Stress Test:** Includes a test case with 50,000 character text nodes to prevent Stack Overflow issues.

### Rationale:
This ensures that the add-in remains stable even when encountering corrupted documents or unexpected XML tags from other plugins.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Unit Tests (npm test)
- [ ] E2E Tests
- [ ] Manual Verification in Word

## ✨ Summary

<!-- Provide a short, clear summary of what this PR does. Keep it concise but informative. -->
Users May have use cases where want to use different search metrics, i.e. dotprod, cosine (normalised dotprod), to do this we have added a scoring method attribute to the vectorstore that is accessed in search to calculate the desired metric.

The scoring logic has been abstracted out to a `score` method to return scored output on given query using the vectorstores chosen metric
We have created a type alias of a literal with all metrics for typehints and checking

body:
Complete Python application for AI-powered blog article generation and automated Blogger API posting. Designed for Termux (Android) with console-based OAuth and comprehensive Plus UI theme component support.

## Architecture

**Core modules:**
- `blogger_api.py` - Blogger API v3 client with OAuth console flow, draft management (create, list, update, publish, delete)
- `ai_generator.py` - Content generation via OpenAI/Gemini with structured JSON output (title, content, labels, meta_description)
- `templates.py` - 36 template methods implementing all Plus UI components (19 categories, 100+ CSS classes)
- `main.py` - CLI application with interactive menu mode and argparse for quick operations
- `config.py` - Centralized configuration with complete Plus UI class mappings

## Key Implementation Details

**Plus UI Components:**
Implemented full component library including: paragraphs (indent, dropcap, reference), images (grid, lazy, scroll), buttons, download boxes, alerts, tables, code blocks, accordions, TOC, related posts, video embeds.

**AI Integration:**
System prompt includes comprehensive Plus UI HTML examples. Parser handles markdown-wrapped JSON responses. Supports both OpenAI (GPT-3.5/4) and Gemini API.

**OAuth Flow:**
Console-based authentication (`run_console()`) for Termux compatibility. Token persistence via `token.json` with automatic refresh.

**CLI Modes:**
- Interactive: 6-option menu (generate, manual post, list drafts, show components, test templates, exit)
- Quick: `--prompt`, `--title`, `--labels` for one-line generation
- Utility: `--list-drafts`, `--components`, `--version`

## Example Usage

```python
# Template usage
from templates import PlusUITemplates
html = PlusUITemplates.alert("Important note", "warning", outlined=True)
html = PlusUITemplates.table(["Name", "Age"], [["Alice", "25"]], bordered=True)

# API usage
from blogger_api import BloggerAPI
api = BloggerAPI()
api.create_draft(title, content, labels)  # isDraft=True
```

```bash
# CLI usage
python main.py --interactive
python main.py --prompt "Python async/await tutorial" --labels "python,tutorial"
python main.py --list-drafts
```

## Security

`.gitignore` configured to exclude `credentials.json` and `token.json`. All Python files include author attribution header with MIT license and "NOT FOR SALE" disclaimer.

## Documentation

Bilingual README (Indonesian/English) with step-by-step Google OAuth setup, Termux installation guide, configuration instructions, and comprehensive Plus UI component reference table.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: Reverse Tabnabbing. Multiple external links using `target="_blank"` were missing `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. This allows the target page to manipulate the `window.opener` object, potentially redirecting the user to a malicious site.
🎯 Impact: If a user clicks an external link to a compromised site, that site could redirect the original tab to a phishing page.
🔧 Fix: Added `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to all static links in `index.html` and updated the JavaScript template literal in `js/main.js` that generates project cards.
✅ Verification: Verified using a custom Playwright script (`verify_security.py`) that scanned all `<a>` tags for the vulnerability. Visual inspection confirmed no layout regressions.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent leaking runtime secrets and avoid blank or crashing UI when required Lovable env vars are missing. 
- Ensure protected Supabase edge-functions are called with the user JWT and surface clear, user-friendly errors for 401/403/5xx conditions. 
- Introduce typed helpers for agent tasks and workflow task plans to improve runtime robustness and validation. 
- Provide docs and a smoke-test checklist for a safe Lovable push/deploy workflow.

### Description
- Env safety and docs: stop tracking `.env`, add `.env.example`, update `.gitignore`, and include `ENV.md` and `SMOKE_TEST_LOVABLE.md`, plus extract a reusable `MissingEnvScreen` component and wire it into `src/main.tsx` to render when required `VITE_*` vars are missing. 
- Edge-function auth & error handling: attach `Authorization: Bearer <user_jwt>` (when a session token exists) and map response statuses to friendly messages across frontend components (`AIAssistant`, `AgentTestChat`, `AIChat`, `AgentChatPanel`, `WorkflowBuilder`, `UploadDocumentDialog`, `ApiKeyManager`, `RecentWorkflows`, `AgentTestChatDialog`, etc.).

author: jey3dayo
body:
## 概要

next-themesを使用してダークモード/ライトモード切り替え機能を実装しました。

## 変更内容

### 依存関係
- `next-themes@0.4.6` をインストール

### コンポーネント
- **ThemeProvider**: next-themesのラッパー（Client Component）
  - `attribute="class"`: Tailwind CSSのdark:クラスと連携
  - `defaultTheme="system"`: システム設定をデフォルトに
  - `enableSystem`: システム設定を有効化
  - `disableTransitionOnChange`: 切り替え時のちらつき防止

- **ThemeSwitcher**: テーマ切り替えボタン（Client Component）
  - Light/Dark/Systemの3つから選択
  - 現在のテーマを視覚的に表示
  - ハイドレーション完了前は読み込み中表示

### スタイル更新
- **Tailwind CSS設定**
  - `darkMode: 'class'` を有効化
  
- **layout.tsx**
  - `ThemeProvider`で全体をラップ
  - `html`タグに`suppressHydrationWarning`追加
  - `themeColor`を動的設定（light: #f8fafc, dark: #0f172a）
  
- **ホームページ**
  - 背景: light時は`from-slate-50 to-slate-100`
  - テキスト: `text-slate-900 dark:text-white`
  - ボタン: ライトモードでも見やすいスタイル
  
- **ダッシュボード**
  - ThemeSwitcherをナビゲーションバーに追加
  - 全要素にdark:クラスを追加
  - ライトモード時の配色を調整

## 技術的特徴

### ハイドレーション対策
- `suppressHydrationWarning`: サーバーとクライアントでテーマが異なる場合の警告を抑制
- `mounted`状態チェック: ハイドレーション完了前は仮表示

### アクセシビリティ
- `aria-label`で各ボタンの役割を明示
- システム設定の自動検出（`prefers-color-scheme`）

### パフォーマンス
- `disableTransitionOnChange`: テーマ切り替え時のトランジションを無効化
- Client Component最小化: ThemeProviderとThemeSwitcherのみ

## テスト

```bash
# 型チェック
pnpm tsc --noEmit

# テスト実行
pnpm test:run

# Lint
pnpm run lint:fix
```

## 動作確認

1. ダッシュボードのナビゲーションバーにテーマ切り替えボタンが表示される
2. Light/Dark/Systemボタンをクリック
3. テーマが即座に切り替わり、選択中のボタンがハイライト表示される
4. ページ全体の配色が切り替わる

## 注意事項

- PR #13（習慣作成機能）とは独立しているため、先にマージ可能
- PR #13マージ後、HabitForm/HabitListClientにもdark:クラスを追加する必要あり

author: tomm789
body:
### Motivation
- Make the outfit-generation experience feel faster and more glamorous by breaking the render modal into many short, rotating steps and richer copy. 
- Surface clearer progress context while a render is pending so users remain on the same page until the job finishes. 
- Preserve navigation/list context when drilling into an outfit so users can move left/right through the list without losing filters or return targets.

### Description
- Added a `generationSteps` array and `generationStepIndex` state that cycles every 2s while `isGeneratingOutfitRender` is active, and reset when the modal closes, controlled in `app/outfits/[id]/view.tsx` via a new `useEffect` timer. 
- Replaced the static modal text with dynamic `title`, `message`, and `subtext` pulled from the active step, and rendered a step list with active highlighting and helper copy inside the generation modal, plus accompanying styles (`loadingDialogStep*`, `loadingDialogSteps`, etc.). 
- Added outfit navigation context support by reading `outfitIds`, `filters`, and `returnTo` from `useLocalSearchParams`, plus `navigationOutfits`, `loadNavigationOutfits`, `navigateToOutfit`, scroll-into-view logic, and a compact horizontal navigation strip in `app/outfits/[id]/view.tsx`. 
- Minor UX tweak: `handleBackPress` now respects `returnTo`/`outfitIds` so the back flow returns to the originating list when applicable.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for these changes.

author: turbocoder13
body:
## Summary

- Replace `jq` with `sed` for updating manifest.json version fields

## Problem

Even with #9 merged, the release workflow still has a fundamental issue:

1. `jq` rewrites the entire JSON file with its default formatting
2. This produces multi-line arrays that conflict with prettier's compact format
3. The workflow relies on `lintro format` to fix this, but that's fragile

## Solution

Use `sed` for targeted field replacement instead of `jq`:
- Only modifies the `version` and `lastUpdated` fields
- Preserves all existing formatting including compact arrays
- No longer depends on `lintro format` to fix the output

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify linting passes on this PR
- [ ] After merge, manually trigger the release workflow or wait for next feature merge
- [ ] Verify the release PR has correctly formatted manifest.json

author: jbeene89
body:
Split the combined ocean trash/N-body code into two completely separate simulation engines with their own interfaces:

**Ocean Trash Module (NEW - Standalone):**
- ocean_trash_engine.cpp: Fluid dynamics engine for ocean currents and pollution
- ocean-trash-simulator.html: Dedicated ocean trash interface with N-body look/feel
- Uses vortex-based ocean current physics (not gravitational)
- 5 ocean gyres modeling Pacific, Atlantic, Indian garbage patches
- Trash types: bottles, bags, microplastics, debris with varied properties
- Time-travel controls: pollution addition, cleanup, glacial melt
- Current dampening and barrier placement
- Ocean temperature effects on currents
- Clean 35KB WASM module

**N-Body Module (RESTORED - Clean):**
- nbody_engine.cpp: Pure gravitational N-body physics
- Removed all ocean trash code
- Removed environmental controls (dampening, barriers, pollution)
- Back to core features: Galaxy Collision, Solar System, Random Cluster
- Clean 28KB WASM module
- nbody-gravity-ultra.html and nbody-gravity-wasm.html updated to remove ocean controls

**Module Separation Benefits:**
- Clean separation of concerns (gravity vs. fluid dynamics)
- Each module can be developed independently
- Smaller, focused codebases
- Can run standalone or combined
- Reusable components

**Design Consistency:**
- Ocean trash HTML uses same glassmorphism style as N-body
- Ocean-themed colors (teal/blue) vs space colors (purple/cyan)
- Identical control panel layout and interaction patterns
- Same Orbitron/Inter font pairing

All three simulators now standalone:
1. N-body gravitational physics (galaxies, solar systems)
2. Ocean trash fluid dynamics (pollution, currents, climate)
3. Bacteria plastic degradation (temperature, weather, species)

author: macabu
body:
Some packages such as `github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go` are only used by Enterprise test files.

However, because they are imported as blank import `_`, it will execute any `init` function they might have, and thus include them in the production build binary.

With this PR, I created a new file `enterprise_imports_test.go` where you can declare imports for these Enterprise-only && test-only dependencies.

That way, they will NOT be marked as "indirect" in `go.mod`, but will also NOT be included in the production binary.

I also took the opportunity to clean up the `enterprise_imports.go` file, there were a bunch of dependencies that are used in OSS and not needed to be duplicated there.

Interestingly, at least on macOS arm64, the binary is now ever so slightly smaller 😄 
```
Before: 409660866 grafana
After:  409310514 grafana
```

author: fbartoli
body:
## What it solves                                                             
                                                                                
  Proposer delegation (add/remove) fails for nested Safes owned by a 2/N parent 
  Safe. The single EOA signature wrapped in EIP-1271 is insufficient — the      
  delegate API requires all threshold signatures, and there was no mechanism to 
  collect multiple owner signatures before submission.                          
                                                                                
  ## How this PR fixes it                                                       
                                                                                
  Uses the Safe Transaction Service's existing off-chain message infrastructure 
  to collect parent Safe owner signatures:                                      
                                                                                
  1. **Initiator** signs the delegate TypedData as a SafeMessage, creates an    
  off-chain message on the parent Safe with structured `origin` metadata tagging
   it as a `proposer-delegation`                                                
  2. **Co-owners** discover pending delegations on the proposer settings page,  
  sign the same SafeMessage to add their confirmation                           
  3. **On threshold met**, the completed `preparedSignature` is wrapped in      
  EIP-1271 format and submitted to the delegate API                             
                                                                                
  Key changes:                                                                  
  - `UpsertProposer.tsx` / `DeleteProposerDialog.tsx` — branch to multi-sig flow
   when parent threshold > 1, show info alert and success state                 
  - New hooks: `useParentSafeThreshold`, `usePendingDelegations`,               
  `useSubmitDelegation`

author: luca24balboni
body: **Problem Description** The instruction vmv.x.s (vector-to-scalar move) caused a deadlock when executed with `RVD=0` configuration (`ELEN=32`). The system would hang indefinitely waiting for result that would never arrive. **Root Cause** The bug was in spatz_vfu.sv, which used logic based on `vsew` to determine byte-enable masks for scalar operations. Scalar registers always have width `ELEN` (32 bits when `RVD=0`, 64 bits when `RVD=1`). `vsew` describes vector element size (8/16/32/64 bits), but vmv.x.s transfers an entire scalar register (`ELEN` bits), not a vector element (`vsew` bits). **Deadlock Mechanism** With RVD=0 (ELEN=32): 1. The vmv.x.s instruction is decoded with `vsew=EW_8` 2. VFU expects `pending_results = 8'hff` (8 bytes, based on wrong vsew check) 3. IPU produces `result_valid = 4'hf` (4 bytes, limited by `ELEN=32`) 4. Result ready check: `&(result_valid | ~pending_results) = &(4'hf | ~8'hff) = &(0b11110000_1111) = 0` 5. Deadlock: Bits 4-7 never become valid → instruction never completes The bug didn't manifest with `RVD=1` (`ELEN=64`) because the IPU produces 8 bytes, coincidentally matching the incorrect expectation.

### Summary This PR introduces a parallel intrinsic for AES/ECB operations to replace the current per-block processing approach, reducing native call overhead and improving throughput for multi-block operations. ### Problem Except supporting AVX512, The existing AES/ECB implementation suffers from three major performance issues: 1. Excessive stub call overhead: Each 16-byte block requires a separate intrinsic call, resulting in high invocation frequency 2. Inefficient instruction-level parallelism: The serialized block processing fails to fully utilize instruction-level parallelism 3. Redundant setup/teardown: Repeated initialization of encryption state for each block ### Changes Added parallel AES intrinsic implementation ### Testing JMH benchmarks It can bring about a **37.43%** performance improvement. On a Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900HX CPU machine with origin implements: ``` Benchmark Mode Cnt Score Error Units AesTest.test avgt 5 11518.846 ± 68.621 ns/op ``` On the same machine with optimized implements: ``` Benchmark Mode Cnt Score Error Units AesTest.test avgt 5 8381.499 ± 57.751 ns/op ``` All Tier-1 tests pass on linux-x64. This modification does not involve changing the encryption or decryption logic. --------- ### Progress - [x] Change must be properly reviewed (1 review required, with at least 1 [Reviewer](https://openjdk.org/bylaws#reviewer)) - [x] Change must not contain extraneous whitespace - [x] Commit message must refer to an issue ### Issue * [JDK-8376164](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8376164): Optimize AES/ECB implementation using full-message intrinsic stub and parallel RoundKey addition (**Enhancement** - P4) ### Reviewers * [Shawn Emery](https://openjdk.org/census#semery) (@smemery - Author) Review applies to [a1976f38](https://git.openjdk.org/jdk/pull/29385/files/a1976f3878bf57a2d7d808d2253c90a3c2ac3ebc) * [Sandhya Viswanathan](https://openjdk.org/census#sviswanathan) (@sviswa7 - **Reviewer**) ### Reviewing

- Convert InsertFloorPlan from mouse events to pointer events for touch device support
- Add `touch-action: none` to prevent browser scroll during drag on floor plan
- Add confirmation dialogs before destructive actions (clear all inserts, delete preset)
- Add toast feedback to design list actions (load, create, delete, error)

- `onMouseDown/Move/Up` → `onPointerDown/Move/Up` with `setPointerCapture`

### Destructive action safety
- Clear all inserts: `window.confirm` + count in message
- Delete user preset: `window.confirm` + name in message
- Both show success toasts after action

### Feedback gaps
- DesignListDialog: toast on load, create, delete success, delete error
- InsertsSection: toast after clearing all inserts
- PresetSelector: toast after deleting a preset

author: podyumkiralama
body:
### Motivation
- Add targeted informational blocks about organization, weddings, large-scale events, and the importance of professional tent rental to enrich the guide content for visitors. 
- Publish updated 2026 tent rental pricing and show size-based fixed rates plus a per‑m² option for large tents so displayed prices match structured data. 
- Improve page flow and media handling by supporting multiple video embeds and keeping structured data in sync with public rates.

### Description
- Inserted four event-focused content blocks into the `Articles` section in `app/(tr)/cadir-kiralama/page.js` to cover organization tents, wedding/ private events, large-scale/corporate projects, and a professional closing note. 
- Added a `PRICING_ITEMS` array and a new `PricingSection` component in `app/(tr)/cadir-kiralama/page.js`, and placed `<PricingSection />` after `Services` in the page flow. 
- Reworked video embedding by replacing the single `VIDEO_EMBED` with `VIDEO_EMBEDS` and mapping over them to render multiple `VideoEmbed` cards. 
- Updated structured data in `lib/structuredData/serviceProducts.js` to set `baseOffers` m² price to `430` and replaced the tent product entries with itemized SKUs and prices (`cadir-5x5`, `cadir-4x4`, `cadir-3x3`, and `cadir-buyuk-olcek`) to match the visible pricing. 

### Testing
- Started the dev server with `npm run dev -- --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000` and the app compiled and served the site successfully (Next dev ready). 
- Loaded `http://127.0.0.1:3000/cadir-kiralama` and received an HTTP 200 response confirming the page rendered. 
- Ran a Playwright script that captured a full-page screenshot saved to `artifacts/cadir-kiralama-articles.png`, and the screenshot step completed successfully.

author: gibs-development
body:
### Motivation
- Improve player feedback by animating the completion toast (slide-in/hold/slide-out) and extending its visible duration, and ensure Vykna progression state is persisted across logins to avoid lost progress.

### Description
- Client: added toast positioning/offset API and exposed panel height in `AchievementCompleteToast` and implemented slide/hold/slide animation and timing in `Client` (new constants `TOAST_SLIDE_TICKS`, `TOAST_HOLD_TICKS` and offset bookkeeping), and updated `showAchievementCompleteToast` to initialize the animated state; key files: `Vykna Client/src/main/java/com/client/graphics/interfaces/impl/AchievementCompleteToast.java` and `Vykna Client/src/main/java/com/client/Client.java`.
- Server: increased the server toast display window to match the longer client animation by adjusting `VyknaProgressionToast` duration; key file: `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/content/vykna_progression/VyknaProgressionToast.java`.
- Persistence: added a versioned JSON persistence layer (`VyknaProgressionPersistence`, `VyknaProgressionSaveData`) and extended `VyknaProgressionPlayerState` to track completion timestamps and dirty/save metadata, with atomic temp-file writes and a single-threaded executor to avoid blocking game threads; key files: `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/content/vykna_progression/VyknaProgressionPersistence.java`, `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/content/vykna_progression/VyknaProgressionSaveData.java`, and `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/content/vykna_progression/VyknaProgressionPlayerState.java`.
- Integration/wiring: centralized completion handling in `VyknaProgressionHandler` via `completeEntry(...)` to record timestamps, award points/score, update leaderboard/summary, trigger the toast, and send a chat message; added save/load hooks so `VyknaProgressionPersistence.load(player)` runs on login and `VyknaProgressionPersistence.save(player, true)` is invoked during the main player save flow; also exposed `getCurrentWalkableInterface()` in `PlayerAssistant` and added toast client ids in `VyknaProgressionInterfaces`; key files: `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/content/vykna_progression/VyknaProgressionHandler.java`, `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/model/entity/player/PlayerAssistant.java`, `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/content/vykna_progression/VyknaProgressionInterfaces.java`, `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/model/entity/player/save/PlayerSave.java`, and `Vykna Gameserver/src/io/xeros/model/entity/player/save/impl/VyknaProgressionSaveEntry.java`.

### Testing
- Built the client with `./gradlew clean build` in `Vykna Client` and the build completed successfully (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`).
- Attempted to run the client with `./gradlew run` but the run failed due to the headless environment (`No X11 DISPLAY variable was set`) so interactive UI verification could not be performed.
- No automated server runtime tests were executed; persistence code is unit-testable but was validated by compilation and integration wiring only.
- Commands executed: `cd "Vykna Client" && ./gradlew clean build` (succeeded) and `cd "Vykna Client" && ./gradlew run` (failed due to headless environment).

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

Model showed 97% accuracy due to two critical data leakage issues:
1. **Look-ahead bias:** Labels used same-day returns, making it a trivial classification task
2. **Temporal leakage:** Random train/test split allowed model to learn from "future" data

## Changes

### Dataset: Next-Day Prediction

Changed label generation from same-day to next-day returns:

```python
# Before: same-day return (look-ahead bias)
stock_return = (close - open_price) / open_price
chosen_stock = sorted(stock_returns)[0]  # best performer today

# After: next-day return (proper temporal prediction)
next_day_idx = day_idx + 1
next_return = (next_close - next_open) / next_open
chosen_stock = sorted(next_day_returns)[0]  # best performer tomorrow
```

**Implementation:**
- Reserve `seq_len + 1` days in sequences (line 216)
- Process only `seq_len` days for features (line 223)
- Calculate labels from day `t+1` data (lines 322-343)

### Temporal Train/Val/Test Split

Replaced random split with chronological split to prevent temporal leakage:

```python
# Before: random split (temporal leakage)
train_dataset, val_dataset = random_split(full_dataset, [0.8, 0.2])

# After: temporal split (no leakage)
train_indices = range(0, int(0.70 * total))      # oldest 70%
val_indices = range(int(0.70 * total), int(0.85 * total))  # middle 15%
test_indices = range(int(0.85 * total), total)   # newest 15% (unseen future)
```

**Location:** Cell 2, lines 387-428

### Evaluation: Updated All Cells to Use Temporal Test Set

Added comprehensive evaluation cell (Cell 12, 276 lines) and updated existing evaluation cells to ensure consistent methodology:

**Cell 7 (Evaluation & Visualization):**
- Changed from `val_loader` to `test_loader`
- All metrics now computed on temporal test set

**Cell 8 (Portfolio Allocation):**
- Changed from `val_dataset` to `test_dataset`  
- Portfolio backtesting now on temporal test set

**Cell 12 (Comprehensive Evaluation):**
- Top-1 and Top-3 accuracy on temporal test set
- Per-stock performance analysis
- Confidence calibration plots
- Confusion matrix visualization

All evaluation cells now consistently use the temporal test set (unseen future data) for final performance metrics, while validation set is properly reserved for early stopping during training.

## Expected Impact

- **Accuracy:** 97% → 45-55% (realistic for stock prediction)
- **Baseline comparison:** 15-20x better than random (2-3%)
- **Methodology:** Now defensible for academic publication
- **Consistency:** All evaluations use same temporal test set

## Files Changed

- `STOCK_MTORL.ipynb`: Cell 2 (dataset fixes), Cells 7-8 (evaluation updates), Cell 12 (new evaluation)
- `FIXES_SUMMARY.md`, `VALIDATION_REPORT.md`, `QUICK_REFERENCE.md`, `EVALUATION_CELLS_UPDATE.md`: Documentation
- `README.md`: Updated project overview
- `.gitignore`: Added

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Critical Issues to Fix
> 
> Your professor is correct - the model showing 97% accuracy while individual components show ~40% is a red flag. After reviewing the code, I've identified **severe data leakage** and evaluation issues.
> 
> ## Problems Identified
> 
> ### 1. **CRITICAL: Look-Ahead Bias / Data Leakage (Lines 680-801 in STOCK_MTORL.ipynb)**
> 
> **Current Issue:**
> ```python
> # Line 701: Calculate return for the SAME DAY
> stock_return = (close - open_price) / open_price
> 
> # Lines 780-786: Select the best stock that ALREADY performed best TODAY
> stock_returns_sorted = sorted(stock_returns, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
> chosen_stock = stock_returns_sorted[0][0]  # This already happened!
> action = self.stock_to_idx[chosen_stock]
> ```
> 
> **Problem:** The model is learning "Given today's market features, pick the stock that performed best TODAY". This is using future information - the model already knows which stock won!
> 
> **Fix Required:** Predict NEXT day's best stock, not today's. The model should use features from day `t` to predict which stock will perform best on day `t+1`.
> 
> ### 2. **No Temporal Train/Test Split (Lines 834-849)**
> 
> **Current Issue:**
> ```python
> # Lines 671-677: Random sampling from entire dataset
> start_idx = np.random.randint(0, max_start + 1)
> ```
> 
> **Problem:** Training and test data contain overlapping time periods. The model sees "future" market conditions during training.
> 
> **Fix Required:** 
> - Train on dates: Start → 70% mark
> - Validation: 70% → 85%  
> - Test: Last 15% (completely unseen future data)
> 
> ### 3. **Unfair Model Comparison**
> 
> **Problem:** We don't see in the notebook where TCN, Attention, and MTORL are evaluated on the SAME held-out test set with the SAME methodology.
> 
> **Fix Required:** Evaluate all three models on identical test data with identical metrics.
> 
> ### 4. **Misleading Accuracy Metric**
> 
> **Current Issue:** 100% accuracy suggests the model is being tested on training data or has data leakage.
> 
> **Fix Required:** Proper evaluation on temporal test set. Expected realistic accuracy: 40-55% (which is actually good for stock prediction!)
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Required Code Changes
> 
> ### Change 1: Fix Dataset Class to Predict Next Day
> 
> In `YahooFinanceDataset.__init__()`:
> 
> 1. **Sequence length adjustment:** When creating sequences, ensure we have day `t+1` available for labels
> 2. **Label creation logic:** 
>    - Use features from day `t` 
>    - Calculate which stock performs best on day `t+1`
>    - That becomes the label
> 3. **Remove same-day labeling**
> 
> ### Change 2: Implement Proper Temporal Split
> 
> Replace the current random split with:
> 
> ```python
> # Sort data by date first
> # Split into:
> # - train_data: first 70% of dates
> # - val_data: next 15% of dates  
> # - test_data: last 15% of dates (future unseen)
> ```
> 
> ### Change 3: Add Fair Evaluation Section
> 
> Add a new evaluation cell that:
> 1. Loads/trains TCN model → evaluates on test set
> 2. Loads/trains Attention model → evaluates on same test set
> 3. Loads/trains MTORL model → evaluates on same test set
> 4. Compares all three with identical metrics
> 
> ### Change 4: Add Realistic Evaluation Metrics
> 
> Add proper evaluation code:
> - Accuracy on temporal test set
> - Top-3 accuracy (is correct stock in top 3 predictions?)
> - Average return if following model's recommendations
> - Confusion analysis
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Expected Results After Fix
> 
> - **TCN Model:** ~38-45% accuracy
> - **Attention Model:** ~38-42% accuracy  
> - **MTORL Combined:** ~45-55% accuracy (modest improvement, not 97%)
> 
> These realistic numbers will be acceptable to your professor because:
> 1. No data leakage
> 2. Proper temporal evaluation
> 3. Fair comparison methodology
> 4. Stock prediction is inherently difficult - 45-55% is actually impressive!
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Implementation Requirements
> 
> Please fix the following files:
> 1. **STOCK_MTORL.ipynb:** Main notebook with all the issues above
> 
> Make sure to:
> - Keep all existing model architectures (TCN, Attention, MTORL)
> - Maintain the stock data loading logic
> - Add clear comments explaining the fixes
> - Add a comprehensive evaluation section comparing all models fairly
> - Include visualization of results
> 
> The goal is to make the evaluation methodology rigorous and defensible for your research paper.


</details>

## What Changed

* Added new environment variable `GO_BROADCAST_AI_FAIL_ON_ERROR` to `.github/.env.base` with default value `false`, controlling error handling behavior for AI failures during sync operations
* Added documentation comments explaining that when true, AI failures cause sync to fail with error messages showing which API key environment variable was used; when false (default), AI failures silently fall back to static templates
* Updated `actions/checkout` action across 24 workflow files from commit `8e8c483db84b4bee98b60c0593521ed34d9990e8` (v6.0.1) to `de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd` (v6.0.2)

## Why It Was Necessary

* Provides operators with configurable control over AI service failure behavior, enabling strict error reporting when debugging API key or service connectivity issues
* Maintains backward compatibility with existing deployments through the default `false` value, ensuring AI failures don't break existing workflows
* Updates checkout action to latest patch version for security and bug fixes across all GitHub Actions workflows

## Testing Performed

* Verified environment variable syntax and formatting in `.env.base` follows existing conventions
* Confirmed all 24 workflow files successfully updated with consistent checkout action version
* Validated default `false` behavior maintains existing silent fallback functionality for AI failures

## Impact / Risk

* **Low Risk**: New feature flag defaults to existing behavior (silent fallback), preventing breaking changes
* **Configuration Change**: Operators can now opt-in to strict AI error reporting by setting `GO_BROADCAST_AI_FAIL_ON_ERROR=true`
* **Action Update**: Checkout action patch version bump (v6.0.1 → v6.0.2) carries minimal risk as patch versions typically contain only bug fixes

author: joshuarileydev
body:
## Summary
Fixes two issues with the queue auto-promotion system:
- Max parallel tasks setting not being respected (e.g., 3 tasks moved to in_progress when max is 2)
- UI not updating automatically after queue promotion (requires manual refresh button press)

## Changes

### Fix 1: Max Parallel Tasks Enforcement
**Problem**: When bulk moving tasks to queue, all tasks would be promoted to in_progress regardless of the `max_parallel_tasks` setting.

**Root Cause**: The `processQueue()` function calculated the in-progress count from the Zustand store on each loop iteration. However, store updates happen asynchronously via IPC events (batched with 16ms delay). This caused the capacity check to use stale state, allowing more tasks than configured to be promoted.

**Fix**: Track promotions locally with `promotedInThisCall` counter instead of relying on store state. The capacity check now uses `initialInProgressCount + promotedInThisCall`.

### Fix 2: Auto-Refresh UI After Queue Promotion
**Problem**: After queue auto-promotion completed, the UI wouldn't reflect the new task statuses until the user manually clicked the refresh button.

**Root Cause**: The backend's `TASK_UPDATE_STATUS` IPC handler only sends `TASK_STATUS_CHANGE` events back to the renderer when auto-starting a task (lines 818-825 in execution-handlers.ts). For simple status changes (like moving from queue to in_progress for already-started tasks), no IPC event is sent. The local store update happens but doesn't trigger a re-render in all cases.

**Fix**: Call `onRefresh()` after queue processing completes to ensure the UI reflects all backend changes.

## Test Plan
1. Set max parallel tasks to 2 in project settings
2. Bulk move 3+ tasks from backlog to queue
3. Verify only 2 tasks move to in_progress (not 3)
4. Verify UI updates automatically without manual refresh

- Created src/lib/ directory and added experimental sync files:

### Steps of Night (Action Uses) Syncing:
- Fixed: Actions with limited uses (like Steps of Night) were not included in sync messages

### Spell Slots Syncing:
- Fixed: Spell slots required toggling because initialization preferred API values over extension values
- Changed initialization logic to use extension values as source of truth
- Extension state now takes precedence over DiceCloud state on first sync
- Spell slots now sync reliably without needing to toggle

## Summary

- Add `checkHubNotLocked()` to `checkStatusPrerequisites()` to match the behavior of `checkSyncPrerequisites()`
- MCP lock warning now appears in the Readiness section output rather than as a surprise logger warning from CentralHub fallback
- Add test coverage for prerequisites module (12 tests)

## Problem

When MCP server is running, `devac status` showed:
```
[CentralHub] Hub is locked by another process (likely MCP server). Falling back to read-only mode.
```

This warning came from the **reactive fallback** in `CentralHub.init()`, not the **preventive check** in prerequisites. The `checkStatusPrerequisites()` function was missing the hub lock check that `checkSyncPrerequisites()` has.

body: ## Summary Implements a lightweight, local-first session memory system that works across all 17 AI coding agents. ### Key Features - **YAML-based storage** - No databases or external services required - **Three memory layers** - Session (ephemeral), Project (persistent), Global (portable) - **AI-powered compression** - Observations compressed into reusable learnings - **Cross-agent injection** - Relevance-based memory retrieval for any agent - **Progressive disclosure** - Token-efficient retrieval (summary → preview → full) ### Core Modules | Module | Purpose | |--------|---------| | `ObservationStore` | Capture raw session observations | | `LearningStore` | Persist compressed learnings | | `MemoryCompressor` | AI/rule-based compression engine | | `MemoryInjector` | Context-aware memory retrieval | | `MemoryObserver` | Automatic observation capture | ### CLI Commands ```bash skillkit memory status # View memory status skillkit memory search # Search memories skillkit memory list # List learnings skillkit memory compress # Compress observations skillkit memory add # Add manual learning skillkit memory export # Export as skill ``` ### TUI Integration - New Memory screen with tabs (Learnings/Observations/Search) - `useMemory` hook for state management - Updated navigation keybindings ### Code Quality - Replaced nested ternaries with explicit functions - Added named constants for magic numbers - Simplified navigation with lookup map ## Test plan - [x] All 132 memory module tests pass - [x] TUI builds successfully - [x] CLI commands work (`skillkit memory status`) - [ ] Manual TUI testing in terminal --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Major CLI expansion: status, pause/resume, run, test, workflow (create/list/run), marketplace, memory, and agent execution; author: gseoc
body:
Remove parts of the legacy implementation in eth_stm32_hal_common.c for the loading of the MAC address when the device-tree is used. Use net_eth_mac_load() for all these cases that were not destined for production-ready products.

When cfg->mac_cfg.type == NET_ETH_MAC_DEFAULT, it means that neither "zephyr,random-mac-address", "local-mac-address" or "nvmem-cells" device-tree properties were used. For this case, keep the legacy property-less implementation to avoid compilation errors and have a default, backward-compatible case.

**Warning: this commit causes backward compatibility breakage for implementations using "zephyr,random-mac-address" or "local-mac-address" properties.**

This patch can come with an entry in the release note to add the content of the warning.

Follow-up of: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/102403

author: drjesseglass
body:
Adds support for Google's TranslateGemma translation models (55 languages) and consolidates the Gemma model family into a unified module structure.

### Reorganization
gemma.rs → gemma/gemma1.rs
Consolidated gemma2.rs, gemma3.rs, quantized_gemma3.rs under gemma/
Added gemma/mod.rs with re-exports for backward compatibility

TranslateGemma Support

Added gemma/translate_gemma.rs with prompt formatting utilities and ISO 639-1 language codes
Added examples/translate-gemma.rs supporting both full precision and quantized inference

### Bug Fixes

gemma3.rs: Make KV tensors contiguous before cache append (fixes "slice-set only supports contiguous tensors" error with certain GQA ratios)
quantized_gemma3.rs: Added clear_kv_cache() method for multi-turn inference

### Usage Notes

Full precision models auto-download from HuggingFace
Quantized inference requires a local GGUF file via --model-path (no official Google GGUF conversions; community conversions available on HuggingFace)

### Known Issue
Investigation shows gemma3.rs uses GELU while quantized_gemma3.rs uses SiLU. This is a gemma3.rs issue, not specific to TranslateGemma.

This change significantly enhances the calendar's configurability and readability by:
- Adding new flags: `--padding` for horizontal spacing, `--monday` to start the week on Monday, `--no-color` to disable ANSI colors, and `--vertical` for an `ncal`-style display.

- Relocating shared command variables (`calYear`, `calMonth`, `filterName`) to `cmd/date.go` to prevent conflicts and improve modularity. The `now` variable was also centralized in `cmd/list.go`.

Fixed AMOC scraper producing entries with empty fields. Root cause: existing entries weren't AI-extracted (missing API key during initial scrape). Consolidated scraper commands into clearer root-level scripts with improved flow.

## Changes

- **AMOC Fix**: Cleared old AMOC entries, rescraped with proper AI extraction
- **Convex**: Added HTTP endpoints for clearing roaster/inactive data and fixed upsert logic
- **Bug Fixes**: Fixed enrichment check that skipped AI extraction, fixed SPA fallback logic
- **Script Consolidation**: Unified script naming and moved all definitions to root package.json
  - `scrape` = scrape + embed (full flow)
  - `scrape:no-embed` = scrape only
  - `scrape:only-embed` = embed only

## Notes

Removed embedding code from cli.ts to decouple concerns. Users can now run scrape and embed independently for flexibility.

author: copilot
body:
IP whitelist configuration was validated at startup but never enforced. Unauthorized requests reached service methods. No audit trail existed for denied access attempts.

## Changes

**IpWhitelistingInterceptor (new)**
- Intercepts all gRPC requests before service methods
- Extracts client IP from `Grpc.TRANSPORT_ATTR_REMOTE_ADDR`
- Enforces whitelist validation via `IpWhitelistValidator.isIpAllowed()`
- Logs warnings with client IP and attempted method on denial
- Returns `PERMISSION_DENIED` with generic message

**IpWhitelistValidator**
- Added warning log when validation fails: IP address and configured whitelist included for audit

**GrpcServer**
- Registered interceptor in server builder before telemetry interceptor

## Audit Log Example

```
WARN [IpWhitelistValidator] Access denied - IP 203.0.113.1 not found in whitelist. Configured whitelist: [192.168.1.1, 10.0.0.0/8]
WARN [IpWhitelistingInterceptor] IP whitelisting access denied: clientIp=203.0.113.1, method=openjproxy.StatementService/connect
```

## Behavior

- Empty/null whitelist allows all (unchanged)
- CIDR ranges and wildcards work as before
- Error message to client is generic to avoid information disclosure

## Overview
This PR introduces several improvements to the codebase focusing on test stability, linting flexibility, and documentation currency for the v0.9.1 release.

## Changes
- **Tests**: Refactored tests to return `Result` instead of panicking, improving error reporting and handling.
- **Linting**: Updated configuration to allow `unwrap` and `expect` in test files, acknowledging that test code has different constraints than production code.
- **Dependencies**: Updated dependencies and enhanced linting configurations across multiple crates.
- **Documentation**: Updated `CURRENT_STATUS.md` and `ROADMAP.md` to reflect the latest progress on v0.9.1 and security hardening.
- **Fixes**: Corrected import paths and enhanced shared output buffer creation in tests.

## Motivation
These changes are part of the production hardening process for v0.9.1, ensuring that the test suite is more robust and that documentation accurately reflects the current state of the project.

body:
Fixes #undefined

## 🎉 Overview

This PR implements the complete **VOZY - Voice Agent AI Platform** for Telconet Ecuador, including:
- **Phase 1**: Foundation, UC-01 Router Configurable, UC-04 History Service
- **Phase 2**: UC-02 Resolve System with UNKNOWN enforcement

## 📦 What's Included

### Infrastructure & Foundation (Tasks 0-1)
- ✅ Monorepo structure (NestJS + Angular 15 + LangGraph Python)
- ✅ Docker Compose (PostgreSQL 15, Redis 7, MinIO, PgAdmin)
- ✅ Prisma ORM with 24 tables (12 Phase 1 + 6 Phase 2 + 6 base)
- ✅ JWT Authentication + RBAC (6 roles, 10 permissions)
- ✅ API Gateway with rate limiting, audit logging, PII masking

### UC-01: Router Configurable (Tasks 2-5, 8)
- ✅ Session Service + Routing Service (deterministic canary deployment)
- ✅ PBX & WhatsApp adapters with idempotent session normalization
- ✅ LangGraph Router Runtime (Python FastAPI) with 3 classification modes
- ✅ Frontend Router Builder UI (Angular 15 + Kendo UI)
- ✅ **UNKNOWN route enforcement** (blocking validation V-ROUTER-03)
- ✅ 17 E2E tests passing

### UC-02: Resolve System (Tasks 9-18)
- ✅ Resolve Config Service with 5 blocking validations (V-RES-UNK-01 to V-RES-UNK-05)
- ✅ Resolve Runtime Service (canary + LangGraph integration + persistence)
- ✅ Simulation Service (dry-run testing before publish)
- ✅ **UNKNOWN route with 3 entry conditions** (low confidence, no evidence, disallowed intent)
- ✅ Tool calls & RAG retrievals tracking (full traceability)
- ✅ 9 REST API endpoints with Swagger docs

### UC-04: History Service (Tasks 6-7)
- ✅ History Query Service (paginated search, max 90 days enforcement)
- ✅ History Detail Service (PII masking, signed audio URLs)
- ✅ Non-blocking audit logging (HISTORY_LIST_VIEW, HISTORY_DETAIL_VIEW)
- ✅ Frontend History UI (2-column layout + turn-by-turn timeline)
- ✅ Materialized view refresh job (hourly cron)

## 🔐 Security & Compliance

- **RBAC**: 6 roles (SYSTEM_ADMIN, TENANT_ADMIN, SUPERVISOR, AGENT, QA, VIEWER)
- **PII Masking**: Role-based, automatic (backend + frontend layers)
- **Auditoría**: Non-blocking, automatic logging of all history accesses
- **Signed URLs**: Temporary audio access (S3/MinIO pre-signed, 1 hour expiry)
- **Rate Limiting**: 100 req/60s (ThrottlerModule)

## 🎯 Key Features

### Router System
- Config-driven routing (no code changes)
- Deterministic canary: `hash(session_id) % 100 < percentage`
- UNKNOWN route mandatory (V-ROUTER-03 blocks publish without it)
- Version lifecycle: DRAFT → ACTIVE → ARCHIVED

### Resolve System
- Config-driven resolve routes (similar to router)
- UNKNOWN route with 3 entry conditions enforced (V-RES-UNK-04)
- Only safe steps allowed in UNKNOWN route (V-RES-UNK-05)
- Tool calls & RAG retrievals fully tracked
- Simulation mode for testing before publish

### History System
- Max 90 days per query (performance enforcement)
- PII masking by default (security first)
- Full audit trail (7 years retention)
- Timeline visualization (turn-by-turn)

## 📊 Technical Stack

**Backend:**
- NestJS 10.3.0 (monorepo with 4 microservices)
- Prisma 5.8.0 ORM
- PostgreSQL 15
- Redis 7
- JWT + Passport

**Frontend:**
- Angular 15.2.10
- Kendo UI for Angular
- Dark theme (modern UI)

**Python Services:**
- LangGraph 0.2.0
- FastAPI 0.109.0
- Structlog (JSON logging)

## 🧪 Testing

- ✅ 17 E2E tests (Phase 1)
- ✅ 9 test scenarios + 2 integration tests (Phase 2)
- ✅ All acceptance criteria validated (CA-01 to CA-04, CA-RES-01 to CA-RES-05)

## 📝 Documentation

Complete technical documentation created:
- `SETUP.md` - Phase 1 setup guide
- `RBAC_SETUP.md` - RBAC implementation (456 lines)
- `ADAPTERS_SETUP.md` - Adapters layer (655 lines)
- `SESSION_SERVICE_SETUP.md` - Session & Routing (600+ lines)
- `HISTORY_SERVICE_SETUP.md` - History service (650+ lines)
- `RESOLVE_SERVICE_SETUP.md` - Resolve service (800+ lines)
- `PRISMA_MIGRATION_INSTRUCTIONS.md` - Migration guide
- `RESOLVE_SERVICE_TESTING.md` - Testing guide

## 🚀 Deployment

**Services:**
- API Gateway: `http://localhost:3000` (Swagger: `/api/docs`)
- Session Service: `http://localhost:3001`
- History Service: `http://localhost:3002`
- Resolve Service: `http://localhost:3003`
- LangGraph Runtime: `http://localhost:8000`
- Frontend: `http://localhost:4200`

**Database:**
- PostgreSQL: `localhost:5432`
- PgAdmin: `http://localhost:5050`
- MinIO: `http://localhost:9001`

## 📈 Metrics

- **Files Created**: 150+ files
- **Lines of Code**: ~15,000+ lines
- **Services**: 13 backend services
- **REST Endpoints**: 30+ endpoints
- **Database Tables**: 24 tables
- **Tests**: 17+ E2E tests
- **Documentation**: 9 technical documents (4,000+ lines)

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria Met

**UC-01 Router:**
- [x] CA-01: UNKNOWN route obligatorio (V-ROUTER-03 blocking)
- [x] CA-02: Canary determinístico (hash-based)
- [x] CA-03: Config-driven desde UI
- [x] CA-04: Versioning completo

**UC-02 Resolve:**
- [x] CA-RES-01: UNKNOWN route obligatorio con 3 entry conditions
- [x] CA-RES-02: Canary determinístico (same pattern as router)
- [x] CA-RES-03: Tool calls tracking completo
- [x] CA-RES-04: RAG retrievals tracking completo
- [x] CA-RES-05: Integración con Phase 1 infrastructure

**UC-04 History:**
- [x] Búsqueda paginada con filtros (max 90 días)
- [x] PII masking automático según roles
- [x] Auditoría obligatoria no-bloqueante
- [x] Timeline turn-by-turn visual

## 🔄 Migration Steps

1. Start Docker services: `docker-compose up -d`
2. Install dependencies: `cd backend && npm install`
3. Run migrations: `npx prisma migrate dev --name add_resolve_tables`
4. Generate Prisma client: `npx prisma generate`
5. Seed database: `npx prisma db seed`
6. Start services: `npm run start:all` or individual services

See `PRISMA_MIGRATION_INSTRUCTIONS.md` for detailed steps.

**Phase 1**: ✅ Complete (Tasks 0-8)  
**Phase 2**: ✅ Complete (Tasks 9-18)  
**All 19 Tasks**: ✅ **COMPLETED**

System is production-ready pending:

  Changes Made

  Database Schema (schema.sql, migrate.ts):
  - Added is_temporary (BOOLEAN) - whether portal must be spawned before use
  - Added spawn_trigger_text (VARCHAR) - text to speak to spawn the portal
  - Added duration_seconds (INTEGER) - how long portal remains active

  Shared Types (doors.ts):

  Door Repository (doorRepository.ts):
  - Added new fields to DbDoor, dbToDoor converter, CreateDoorInput, createDoor, and updateDoor

  Door State Manager (doorStateManager.ts):
  - Added activePortals map to track spawned portals
  - Added portalExpirationTimers map for expiration timers
  - New functions: isPortalActive(), spawnPortal(), despawnPortal(), findPortalBySpawnTrigger()
  - Updated canPassThrough() to block inactive temporary portals
  - Updated findSpecialDoorByTrigger() and findSpecialDoorByDisplayName() to only match active portals

  Commands (commands.ts):
  - Added spawn trigger detection before special door triggers
  - Added handlePortalSpawn() function to spawn portals and broadcast appearance

  World (world.ts):
  - Updated "Also here:" display to only show active temporary portals

  Example Usage

  1. Create a temporary portal with door_type='temporary_portal', is_temporary=true, spawn_trigger_text='Valar Morghulis', trigger_text='go portal', item_display_name='a whirling vortex', duration_seconds=60
  2. Player types "Valar Morghulis" - portal appears: "a whirling vortex appears out of thin air!"
  3. Portal shows on "Also here:" line for 60 seconds
  4. Player types "go portal" to pass through
  5. After 60 seconds: "The a whirling vortex vanishes!"

  # Initial Claude Code Review before submitting PR.

 Issues Found

  1. Bug: Portal vanish message has redundant article (doorStateManager.ts:782-784)

  const message = door.itemDisplayName
    ? `The ${door.itemDisplayName} vanishes!`
    : `The portal vanishes!`;
  If itemDisplayName is "a whirling vortex", the message becomes "The a whirling vortex vanishes!" - a grammatical error.

  2. Bug: Same issue in handlePortalSpawn (commands.ts:1201-1202)

  const portalName = door.itemDisplayName || door.name || 'a portal';
  const appearanceMessage = `${portalName} appears out of thin air!`;
  This produces "a whirling vortex appears out of thin air!" which is correct, but inconsistent with the vanish message format.

  3. Missing cleanup: reloadDoor doesn't clean up portal state (doorStateManager.ts:106-137)

  When a door is deleted via reloadDoor(), the code cancels autoCloseTimer but doesn't cancel portalExpirationTimer or remove from activePortals.

  4. Edge case: Non-temporary TEMPORARY_PORTAL doors

  The code checks door.isTemporary but a TEMPORARY_PORTAL door type with isTemporary=false is an odd configuration. This is handled correctly (treated as always-active), but it's a confusing state.

body:
Stub generator incorrectly marked the first query parameter as "required" for query-only endpoints, ignoring the OpenAPI schema's `required: false` and `default` values.

## Root Cause

In `parse_function_params()`, when `has_path_params = FALSE`, the first query parameter was unconditionally marked as required:

```r
if (!is.null(primary_param) && p_san == primary_param) {
  is_required <- TRUE  # Bug: ignores schema metadata
}
```

This caused `ct_bioactivity_assay(projection = NULL)` instead of `ct_bioactivity_assay(projection = "assay-all")`.

## Changes

- **`dev/endpoint_eval/06_param_parsing.R`**: Only mark primary params as required if schema says `required=true` AND no default value exists
- **`R/ct_bioactivity_assay.R`**: Apply correct default from schema

## Tidy Flag

The `tidy` parameter is intentionally not exposed in generated signatures—it defaults to `TRUE` in `generic_request`. Some endpoints internally use `tidy = FALSE` based on response type, but this is controlled by the generator, not user-configurable. This is by design.

### Motivation
- Remote statblock images fetched from the storage API were being saved to the local `images/` folder, causing unwanted local persistence and cache churn.
- The app should display remote images in-memory without writing to disk unless explicitly enabled via a toggle.

### Description
- Changed remote-image handling in `lib/app/app.py` to load bytes into a `QPixmap` via `pixmap.loadFromData(data)` and avoid always writing to disk.
- Added an environment-gated cache: remote images are only written to disk when `CACHE_REMOTE_IMAGES` is set to `1`; the default is `0` (disabled).
- File changed: `lib/app/app.py` (update in `resize_to_fit_screen` where remote data is handled).
- Previously the code always executed `with open(image_path, "wb") as f: f.write(data)`; it now only performs that write when `os.getenv("CACHE_REMOTE_IMAGES", "0") == "1"` so remote images remain in-memory by default.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a simple "AI 2.0" for enemies that makes 1–3 PA-consuming decisions per turn using a score-based decision system. 
- Keep the AI pure-script (no scene/node dependencies) and reuse existing systems (LOS, pathfinding, abilities, damage) to avoid large API changes. 
- Make enemy behaviour more tactical (shoot/ability/move/overwatch) and add lightweight role/tags metadata for targeting priorities. 

### Description
- Added `res://scripts/tactical/ai.gd` implementing `class_name TacticalAI` and the main entry `TacticalAI.take_turn(controller: TacticalController, enemy: Unit)` which scores and executes actions (`SHOOT`, `ABILITY`, `MOVE`, `OVERWATCH`) while consuming PA and logging choices via `print`. 
- Scoring heuristics implemented for: `SHOOT` (hit chance, estimated damage/kill, low HP, role priority, cover penalty), `ABILITY` (damage, AOE multi-target, CC tags, finishing), `MOVE` (reachable tiles via `Pathfinding.reachable_with_pa`, cover, LOS, high ground, avoid melee if fragile), and `OVERWATCH` (position+cover/LOS fallback). 
- Integrated AI into `TacticalController` by preloading and instantiating `TacticalAI` and calling `_tactical_ai.take_turn(self, act)` on enemy activations, preserving existing controller helper calls (e.g. `_compute_shot_preview`, `_try_attack`, `_try_move_with_overwatch_triggers`, `_cast_*`). 
- Added optional unit metadata in `Unit` (`@export var role: String = ""` and `@export var tags: Array[String] = []`) to allow priority targeting without breaking existing code (backward-compatible defaults). 

### Testing
- No automated tests were run against these changes.

author: todddb
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the chat pipeline to better handle policy-specific questions and improves how sources are displayed and cited in responses. It introduces intent-based policy detection, document aggregation by relevance, and inline citation support throughout the synthesis and validation stages.

## Key Changes

### Intent Analysis
- Added detection logic to distinguish between specific policy questions (e.g., "What is THE remote work policy?") and general definitions (e.g., "What is a remote work policy?")
- Intent context now includes a `specific_policy` flag to guide downstream processing

### Research & Document Aggregation
- Implemented `aggregate_hits_by_doc()` function to consolidate chunk-level search results into document-level results
- Aggregation tracks best score, total score, and match count per document
- Results are sorted by relevance and limited to top 6 documents for synthesis
- Added `AggregatedDocument` schema to represent consolidated results

### Synthesis Pipeline
- Updated `synthesize_answer()` to accept aggregated documents and generate inline citations
- Added context-aware instructions: specific policy questions now require citations and focus on provided sources only
- Synthesis output now includes numbered source references [1], [2], etc.
- Policy questions receive stricter instructions to avoid hallucination

### Validation Pipeline
- Enhanced `validate_answer()` to check for presence of inline citations
- Added warning flag when specific policy questions lack citations
- Validation now receives intent context to apply appropriate checks

### Chat Route
- Integrated document aggregation into the chat flow
- Passes aggregated docs to synthesis and intent context to validation
- Response now includes both legacy citations and new aggregated sources for frontend compatibility

### Frontend UI
- Redesigned sources panel with inline display of top 3 sources
- Added expandable "More sources" section for additional results
- Improved visual hierarchy with numbered badges, snippets, and metadata
- New CSS classes for better styling and responsive layout

## Implementation Details
- Maintains backward compatibility by keeping original hits-based citations alongside new aggregated sources
- Policy detection uses simple string matching on context field for reliability
- Document aggregation preserves snippet from highest-scoring chunk for each document
- Frontend gracefully falls back to old format if new sources unavailable

## CI Test Timeout and Failure Fix - TypeScript Errors Fixed

### Latest Change - TypeScript Errors Fixed ✅

**Issue**: TypeScript compilation failed with errors in `test-providers.tsx`
- Properties `categoryId`, `subcategoryId`, `difficultyLevel`, and `tenantId` did not exist on inferred type `{ id: number }`

----

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>CI Job Fails: Multiple Test Failures and Workflow Timeout (Patch Firestore Connection & Integration Mocks)</issue_title>
<issue_description>## Job Failure: Multiple Test Suites and Workflow Timeout

During a CI job in `archubbuck/certlab`, several test suites failed and the overall process exceeded the workflow's hard timeout (5 minutes), causing an exit with code 1.

### Root Causes & Code-Based Solutions

#### 1. Slow/Faulty Firestore Connection Handling
- Tests in [`client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.test.ts`](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.test.ts) show timeouts:
  > `[Firestore Connection] Check failed: Error: Connection check timeout`
- The hook uses a 5s timeout for health checks ([source](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.ts#L137-L162)), repeatedly entering error/reconnection.
  - Health checks use a snapshot on `categories` ([see code](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.ts#L137-L162)), and reconnect attempts use exponential backoff capped at 30s ([see code](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.test.ts#L462-L480)).
  - Tests mock errors to force reconnection ([see code](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.test.ts#L411-L436)).
- **Remediations:**
  - Patch seeds/mocks so `categories` collection always exists in CI/test environments to avoid unnecessary timeouts.
  - Add a fast-mock mode: Skip real connection test and set `status` to "connected" when `process.env.CI` is present.
  - Review teardown logic to clean up intervals/timeouts after tests ([see teardown code](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.ts#L373-L405)).

#### 2. Failing Integration Tests
- Integration failures reported in tests such as:
  - [`quiz-flow.test.ts`](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d) – quiz questions not matching criteria
  - `query-cache.test.tsx` – cache/stale queries
  - `auth-flow.test.tsx` – authentication/profile sync
  - `multi-tenant.test.ts` – tenant switching/data isolation ([multi-tenant coverage](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/docs/INTEGRATION_TESTING_SUMMARY.md#L27-L55))
  - `accessibility.test.tsx` – navigation
- Tests rely on seeds and reset mocks ([example](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/docs/INTEGRATION_TESTING_SUMMARY.md#L27-L55)) but may not be re-seeding consistently between test suites.
- **Remediations:**
  - Ensure every test suite sets up/tears down consistent Firestore mock data before each test (`resetIntegrationMocks`, `seedTestData`).
  - Patch implementations so categories, users, and quiz entities are always present in test runs.
  - Mock responses aggressively for CI: reduce dependence on emulator speed/availability.

#### 3. Workflow Timeout in CI
- The test step in `.github/workflows/firebase-deploy.yml` imposes 5 minute limit:
  ```yaml
  # Wait for up to 5 minutes
  for i in {1..300}; do ...
  ```
- Integration/emulator-heavy tests can exceed this.
- **Remediations:**
  - Split emulator/integration-heavy tests off to run in a separate block or workflow with longer timeout ([see workflow docs](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/docs/setup/ci-cd-setup.md#L79-L102)).
  - Reduce test concurrency, speed up mocks, or skip flakiest suites for baseline CI.

### Recommended Actions
- Patch test data setup: Always mock `categories` and `users` in Firestore before all integration tests.
- Add CI/test environment detection and "fast mock" mode to `useFirestoreConnection`.
- Split integration/emulator-heavy tests to optional blocks or separate CI workflows with extended timeouts.
- Aggressively mock responses for CI—ensure emulator is running, clean up all intervals/timeouts post-test.
- For persistent failures, comment out the flakiest tests temporarily.

### Code References
- [`useFirestoreConnection.ts`](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.ts) ([health check logic](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.ts#L137-L162), [teardown](https://github.com/archubbuck/certlab/blob/7a43a316d23ccdcc1b7633be0eb68ec414960b9d/client/src/hooks/useFirestoreConnection.ts#L373-L405), [status transitions](https://github.com/archubbu...

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR addresses consistency issues in the `EngineCompat.ExecuteCommand` fallback mechanism.

1.  **Inconsistency in `PLAY_CARD` fallback:** Previously, if `ExecuteCommand` was called with a `PLAY_CARD` command but without a valid `card_db` argument (or if lookup failed), the code defaulted to treating the card as a Creature, placing it in the Battle Zone. This was incorrect for Spells. The fix now attempts to look up the card in the global `dm_ai_module.CardDatabase` (if available) to correctly identify Spells and send them to the Graveyard.
2.  **Missing `EffectResolver` in Stub:** The `dm_ai_module.py` stub lacked the `EffectResolver` class, which `compat.py` explicitly tries to call as a fallback. This PR adds `EffectResolver` to the stub, wrapping `GenericCardSystem.resolve_action` to match the expected signature.

These changes ensure that the fallback chain (C++ -> State -> Command -> EffectResolver -> Python Mutation) works reliably even in pure-Python execution modes.

author: mixaill76
body:
# Changelog Entry

### Description

This pull request adds support for using Active Directory Security Identifier (AD SID) as the user ID in LDAP authentication. This feature allows organizations to maintain consistent user identifiers across systems when using Active Directory, as the AD SID is a unique and immutable identifier for each user object in Active Directory.

When enabled, the LDAP authentication will extract the `objectSid` attribute from AD, convert it to string format (e.g., `S-1-5-21-3396494274-2626632863-120886085-599475`), and use it as the user's ID in Open WebUI instead of generating a random UUID. This provides better integration with AD-based environments and ensures user identity consistency.

**Integration with External Systems:**
This feature is particularly critical when `ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS` is enabled. Open WebUI forwards user information headers (including `X-OpenWebUI-User-Id`) to external services such as:
- TTS/STT providers (for personalization and rate limiting)
- Web search engines
- Document loaders
- LLM backends (Ollama, OpenAI, etc.)

With this feature, external systems will receive the user's AD SID in the `X-OpenWebUI-User-Id` header instead of a random UUID. This enables external systems to:
- Implement user-specific rate limiting based on AD identity
- Track usage and costs per AD user across multiple systems
- Maintain audit logs with consistent AD-based user identifiers
- Integrate with existing enterprise identity management and billing systems
- Correlate user activity across Open WebUI and other corporate applications

### Added

- New configuration parameter `LDAP_USE_AD_SID` to enable/disable AD SID usage for user IDs
- Function `convert_ad_sid_to_string()` to convert binary AD SID to string representation
- Support for `objectSid` attribute in LDAP search queries when AD SID usage is enabled
- Logging for AD SID extraction and conversion process

### Changed

- Modified `AuthsTable.insert_new_auth()` to accept optional `id` parameter instead of always generating UUID
- Updated LDAP authentication flow to extract and use AD SID when `LDAP_USE_AD_SID` is enabled
- Extended LDAP search attributes to include `objectSid` when AD SID feature is enabled

### Deprecated

- None

### Removed

- None

### Fixed

- None

### Security

- None

### Breaking Changes

- None (feature is opt-in via configuration parameter, defaults to disabled)

---

### Additional Information

**Configuration:**
- The feature is controlled by the `LDAP_USE_AD_SID` environment variable (defaults to `False`)
- Can be set via environment variable: `LDAP_USE_AD_SID=true`
- Persisted in config as `ldap.server.use_ad_sid`

**Technical Details:**
- If AD SID extraction fails or is not available, the system falls back to UUID generation with appropriate warning logs
- The AD SID conversion follows the standard Microsoft format: `S-Revision-IdentifierAuthority-SubAuthority1-SubAuthority2-...`
- Extracts the `objectSid` binary attribute from Active Directory
- Converts binary SID using correct byte order: revision (1 byte), sub-authority count (1 byte), identifier authority (6 bytes, big-endian), sub-authorities (4 bytes each, little-endian)

**Use Cases:**
- Organizations using `ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS=True` for external service integration
- Enterprise environments requiring consistent user identification across multiple systems
- Cost tracking and billing per AD user
- Audit and compliance requirements with AD-based user identity
- Integration with existing identity management systems

**Documentation Updates Required:**
- Environment variables documentation: add `LDAP_USE_AD_SID` parameter
- LDAP authentication tutorial: explain when and why to use AD SID
- External service integration guide: explain the relationship with `ENABLE_FORWARD_USER_INFO_HEADERS`

body:
This PR addresses consistency and robustness issues in the `EngineCompat` layer and the pure-Python `dm_ai_module` stub.

**Changes:**
1.  **`dm_ai_module.py`**:
    *   Added `class Phase(IntEnum)` with values `MANA=2`, `MAIN=3`, `ATTACK=4`, `END=5` to align with the C++ engine's phase definitions.
    *   Added `PhaseManager.check_game_over` stub implementation to support game over detection tests.

2.  **`dm_toolkit/engine/compat.py`**:
    *   Improved the "forced progression" logic in `PhaseManager_next_phase`. Previously, it used simple modulo arithmetic `(current + 1) % (max + 1)` which assumed zero-based contiguous phases. This caused a crash (ValueError) when wrapping around from `END` (5) to `MANA` (2) because `0` is not a valid phase.
    *   The new logic sorts the available `Phase` enum values and cycles through them by index, ensuring a valid next phase is always chosen regardless of the underlying integer values.

3.  **Tests**:
    *   Created `tests/test_compat_phase_manager.py` to rigorously test `PhaseManager_start_game`, `PhaseManager_next_phase` (normal, retry, forced), and `PhaseManager_check_game_over`.
    *   Verified that the forced progression logic now correctly handles the `END` -> `MANA` transition.

This ensures that the Python fallback mode is robust and that `EngineCompat` can recover from "stuck" engine states without crashing.

## Summary
Add a new `/review-pr` command to review GitHub pull requests using the `gh` CLI tool.

### Features
- **List PRs**: When no PR number provided, runs `gh pr list` to show available PRs
- **Review PR**: When PR number provided, runs `gh pr view|diff|checks|comment list`
- **Multi-repo support**: Optional repo parameter: `/review-pr <num> [repo]`
- **Standalone commands**: `/review-pr`, `/review-pull-request`, `/git review-pr`

### Review Framework
The command generates comprehensive reviews covering:
1. **Code Quality**: Clarity, maintainability, best practices
2. **Functionality**: Does it solve the intended problem?
3. **Potential Issues**: Bugs, security vulnerabilities, performance concerns
4. **Testing**: Are tests adequate and do they cover edge cases?
5. **Documentation**: Is the code properly documented?

### Changes
- Added `reviewPrPrompt()` function in `src/commands/git-commands.ts`
- Updated help text in `src/index.ts` to distinguish `/review` (local file) from `/review-pr` (GitHub PR)
- Added 12 comprehensive tests in `tests/git-commands.test.ts`
- Registered `reviewPrAlias` command

### Usage Examples
```bash
# List available PRs
/review-pr

# Review a specific PR
/review-pr 42

# Review PR from another repo
/review-pr 42 owner/repo
```

- [x] Code compiles

- [x] Build succeeds

### Motivation
- Nutzer konnten sich trotz korrekter Anmeldedaten nicht per Quick‑Connect verbinden, weil verschiedene AD‑Setups unterschiedliche Principal‑Formate (UPN, NETBIOS\user, plain) erwarten. 
- Die Base DN sollte automatisiert erkannt werden, statt dass Anwender sie manuell eintragen müssen.

### Description
- Ergänzt `build_ad_principals(username, domain)` in `app.py` und passt `authenticate_ad_user` an, um mehrere Principal‑Formate (user@domain, NETBIOS\user, plain) auszuprobieren. 
- Implementiert `domain_to_base_dn` und `discover_base_dn` zur Ermittlung der Base DN über Server‑Info, RootDSE (`BASE`) oder Fallback aus der Domain. 
- Fügt neuen Quick‑Connect Endpoint `POST /api/ad/quick-connect` hinzu, der mit dem ersten erfolgreichen Principal bindet, die Base DN ermittelt und `ad_settings` persistiert. 
- Aktualisiert `templates/users.html` um das Quick‑Connect Formular, Alpine.js State `adQuick` und die Aktion `quickConnectAd()`, sowie einen Hinweistext für `user@domain` oder `DOMAIN\user`.

### Testing
- Entwicklungsserver mit `python app.py` gestartet und der Server lief erfolgreich.

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive formalization of Erdős Problem #789 about sum-length-free subsets.

### The Problem
- h(n) = max |B| such that B ⊆ A, |A| = n, and equal sums in B have equal length
- That is: if a₁+⋯+aᵣ = b₁+⋯+bₛ with aᵢ,bᵢ ∈ B then r = s
- **Question**: Estimate h(n)
- **Status**: OPEN (gap between bounds)

### Known Bounds
- **Upper (Straus 1966)**: h(n) ≪ √n
- **Lower (Erdős-Choi 1974)**: h(n) ≫ (n log n)^{1/3}
- Gap between exponents 1/3 and 1/2 is significant

### Key Formalizations
1. `SumRep` structure for sum representations
2. `SumLengthFree` property definition
3. `h` function axiom with existence proof
4. Upper bounds: `erdos_1962_upper`, `straus_1966_upper`
5. Lower bounds: `erdos_1962_lower`, `erdos_choi_1974_lower`
6. `IsSidonSet` definition with `sidon_implies_sum_length_free`
7. Computational examples with `native_decide`

### Changes
- **Lean proof**: 275-line formalization with no sorries (uses documented axioms)
- **meta.json**: Enhanced with historical context, Sidon connection, Mathlib dependencies
- **annotations.json**: 13 comprehensive annotations

## Test Plan

- [x] meta.json validates correctly

author: gabrielste1n
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes a critical timing issue where file logging was being initialized before the Electron app was ready, causing `app.getPath()` to be called unsafely. The solution defers file logging initialization until after `app.whenReady()` completes.

## Problem
The `debugLogger` module was being loaded transitively through other managers (e.g., `windowManager` → `hotkeyManager` → `debugLogger`) before `app.whenReady()` was called. This caused the constructor to immediately call `initializeFileLogging()`, which uses `app.getPath("userData")` - an unsafe operation before the app is ready.

## Key Changes
- **debugLogger.js**: 
  - Removed immediate `initializeFileLogging()` call from constructor
  - Added `fileLoggingPending` flag to track deferred initialization
  - Added safety check in `initializeFileLogging()` to verify `app.isReady()` before accessing `app.getPath()`
  - Added new `ensureFileLogging()` method to explicitly initialize file logging when safe
  - Added lazy initialization attempt in the `write()` method as a fallback

- **main.js**:
  - Added explicit call to `debugLogger.ensureFileLogging()` in `initializeManagers()` after `app.whenReady()` has completed

## Implementation Details
- File logging initialization is now deferred and happens at the earliest safe moment
- Multiple initialization paths ensure file logging is set up: explicit call via `ensureFileLogging()`, lazy initialization on first log write, or when app becomes ready
- The `fileLoggingPending` flag prevents repeated initialization attempts
- All error states properly reset the pending flag to avoid infinite retry loops

author: copilot
body:
Replaces deprecated `apt-key add` with modern keyring-based repository key management using `/etc/apt/keyrings`.

## Changes

**`.github/nvidia-gpu-setup.md`**
- NVIDIA Docker repository setup now uses GPG keyring files instead of global keystore
- Added error checking for key download and sources.list creation

**`.github/workflows/prune-caches.yml`**
- Creates keyrings directory before apt operations

**`.github/unity-hub-setup.md`** (NEW)
- Comprehensive Unity Hub installation guide using modern APT keyring method
- Includes all required commands for Unity Hub setup:
  - GPG key download and installation
  - Repository configuration with `signed-by` syntax
  - Unity Hub package installation
- Covers verification, usage, troubleshooting, and GPU acceleration setup
- Error checking for robust installation process

**`README.md`**
- Added "Development Tools & Setup Guides" section
- References both Unity Hub and NVIDIA GPU setup guides

## Technical Details

Before (deprecated):
```bash
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | sudo apt-key add -
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list
```

After (modern approach):
```bash
sudo install -d /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/gpgkey | \
  sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/nvidia-docker.gpg
curl -s -L https://nvidia.github.io/nvidia-docker/$distribution/nvidia-docker.list | \
  sed "s#deb https://#deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/nvidia-docker.gpg] https://#g" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nvidia-docker.list
```

Unity Hub setup follows the same modern pattern:
```bash
sudo install -d /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://hub.unity3d.com/linux/keys/public | \
  sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/unityhub.gpg
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/unityhub.gpg] https://hub.unity3d.com/linux/repos/deb stable main" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/unityhub.list
sudo apt update
sudo apt install unityhub
```

Required for Ubuntu 22.04+ where `apt-key` is deprecated. Repository keys are now isolated per-repository rather than in a global keyring.
