body:
This PR migrates the Ren'Py script parsing logic from the backend to the frontend, enabling deterministic layout rendering and persistent drag-and-drop functionality.

Key changes:
1.  **Backend:** Removed `RenPyParser` and related logic from `backend/app/api/routes/scripts.py`. API endpoints now return raw script content instead of a parsed tree.
2.  **Frontend Parser:** Implemented a recursive descent parser in `frontend/src/utils/renpyParser.ts` that matches the original Python logic but runs in the browser. It supports attaching metadata comments (prefixed with `# @NODE`) to the immediately following node block.
3.  **Relative Positioning:** Updated `frontend/src/utils/flowTransformer.ts` to calculate node positions based on a logical layout plus a relative offset stored in metadata. This ensures that moving a parent node (changing its offset) dynamically moves its entire subtree while maintaining relative structure.
4.  **Persistence:** Implemented `onNodeDragStop` in `EditorPage.tsx`. When a node is dragged, the new relative offset is calculated and written back to the script file as a metadata comment (`offset="x,y"`), ensuring positions persist across reloads.
5.  **Metadata Handling:** Enhanced `frontend/src/utils/nodeMetadata.ts` to parse and format `offset` and `uuid` fields in metadata comments.

This change reduces server load, improves interactivity, and fulfills the requirement for client-side control over graph presentation.

author: ghislainbourgeois
body:
# Description

This PR adds an include/exclude mechanism for tests. If `--include` is specified, only tests that have ID that contain any of the `include` substrings will be selected. If `--exclude` is specified, tests that have ID that contain any of the `exclude` substrings will be deselected. 

They can be combined in powerful ways, for example running all gNodeB tests, except the sctp test can be done with: `-i "gnb/" -e "sctp"`.

Both options can be specified multiple times: `-i "ue/registration" -i "ue/authentication"`.

The `--environment` argument is also removed with this PR. It was only used to exclude the `ue/paging/downlink_data` test by default, and the new feature allows to explicitly exclude a test instead. While it will be a breaking change, this should not break CI as the version is pinned.

body:
### Motivation
- Improve the offline agent's limited answers by enabling multiple specialized agents to run concurrently and collaborate on a single, higher-quality response.
- Make agent behavior configurable and visible so operators can tune roles and enable/disable collaborative mode via `config.py` and the chat UI.

### Description
- Added `ENABLE_MULTI_AGENT` and `AGENT_ROLES` to `config.py` to declare configurable agent roles, goals and per-role temperatures.
- Implemented parallel multi-agent orchestration in `main.py` using `ThreadPoolExecutor` and new helper methods ` _build_agent_prompt`, `_run_agent`, and `_generate_collaborative_response`, plus integration into `generate_response` for optional synthesis.
- Exposed multi-agent status and a new `agentes` chat command to list configured roles, and updated `README.md` with documentation for the collaborative mode.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: fw-bot
body:
### Steps to reproduce:

- In the settings enable By-Products
- Create a product with an color attribute and 2 values: white, black
- Create a bom for that products and add 2 by product lines:
    - 1 x comp1 with a cost_share of 50% specific to the white att-value
    - 1 x comp2 with a cost_share of 70% specific to the Black att-value
#### > Try to save and you will raise a UserError: The total cost share for a BoM's by-products cannot exceed 100.

### Expected behavior:

The error should not be raised as the total cost_share is 50% for the white variant and 70% for the black one but none of them exceeds the 100% cost share.

### Cause of the Issue:

Currently the constraint does not take attribute values into accounts and simply sums the value of the cost share of all by-product lines: https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/bcc1397c7d694dbe61ecbd44d0320b9518df84cb/addons/mrp/models/mrp_bom.py#L201-L202

### Motivation
- The new toggle card styles were leaking globally and changing the appearance of other cards by applying rules to generic selectors like `ha-card` and `.toggle-*`. 
- That leakage caused unrelated components such as the dashboard background card to break visually. 
- Scope the toggle card styles to its host element so the new visual identity does not affect other cards. 

### Description
- Scoped all CSS rules in `src/cards/toggle/dihor-toggle-card.css` by prefixing selectors with the `dihor-toggle-card` host so styles only apply to the toggle card. 
- Added the toggle card implementation files `src/cards/toggle/dihor-toggle-card.ts`, `src/cards/toggle/dihor-toggle-card.html`, and the scoped stylesheet `src/cards/toggle/dihor-toggle-card.css`. 
- Hooked the new component into the bundle by importing it in `src/index.ts` and exporting `ToggleCard` for direct imports. 
- Implemented `ToggleCard` which validates `entity` in `setConfig`, registers event handlers in `onCardCreated`, updates label/state in `update(hass)`, and calls `hass.callService(domain, "toggle", { entity_id })` in `toggleEntity`. 

### Testing

body:
## Summary

- Simplifies `VersionWarning` component to show a version notice on any versioned subdomain (e.g., `v2-3-1.turborepo.dev`)
- Removes npm registry fetch and version comparison logic that was never working as intended

## Context

The previous implementation tried to fetch the latest version from npm and compare it to the subdomain version to determine if the docs were "old." However, versioned subdomains don't serve archived documentation - they all serve the same latest deployment. The subdomains exist primarily for serving versioned `schema.json` files.

The new behavior simply shows an informational notice with the version number and a link to the main docs site whenever a user is on any versioned subdomain.

author: santhoshbala
body:
## Summary

This PR completes Task 0.3 by evaluating the Congress.gov API (v3) as a data source for bill metadata, legislator information, and sponsor/cosponsor tracking. The evaluation concludes that Congress.gov API is an excellent fit for CWLB's needs and should be the primary source for linking Public Laws to their sponsors and tracking legislative activity.

## Changes

- **Updated TASKS.md**: Marked Task 0.3 as complete and added reference to evaluation document
- **Added TASK-0.3-Congress-API-Evaluation.md**: Comprehensive 1,094-line evaluation document covering:
  - Executive summary with key findings and recommendation
  - API overview and authentication requirements
  - Rate limits (5,000 requests/hour) and coverage analysis
  - Detailed endpoint documentation (Bill, Member, Vote, Actions, etc.)
  - Sponsor and cosponsor data availability (93rd Congress 1973+ for sponsors, 97th Congress 1981+ for dates)
  - Member endpoint coverage (71st Congress 1929+ for members serving in 93rd Congress or later)
  - Vote records status (House votes available 118th Congress 2023+, Senate votes planned)
  - Data quality limitations and historical coverage gaps
  - Comparison with alternative APIs (ProPublica, GovInfo)
  - Integration recommendations for CWLB's data pipeline
  - Usage examples and next steps

## Key Findings

✅ **Recommendation**: Congress.gov API is the preferred primary source for CWLB

**Strengths:**
- Official Library of Congress authoritative data
- Comprehensive bill metadata from 1973 forward
- Rich sponsor/cosponsor data with dates (1981+)
- Complete legislator profiles with photos
- Generous rate limits suitable for batch ingestion
- Free access with well-documented OpenAPI specification

**Limitations:**
- Pre-1973 bills lack sponsor/summary metadata
- Senate votes not yet available via API (XML links provided)
- Member data only includes those serving in 93rd Congress (1973) or later
- Cosponsorship dates unavailable for 1973-1980 period

**Supplements Needed:**
- ProPublica Congress API for Senate votes and voting statistics
- GovInfo API for Public Law text (already covered in Task 0.2)

## Implementation Notes

The evaluation provides:
- Detailed API endpoint specifications with example responses
- Coverage date matrix for all data types
- Data pipeline strategy for three phases (MVP, Enhancement, Open PRs)
- Rate limit optimization guidance
- Error handling recommendations
- Data quality assurance verification strategy
- Immediate action items for prototype development

This document serves as the foundation for Phase 1 implementation of the CWLB data ingestion pipeline.

author: hugo-pare
body:
### What is the purpose of this change?

Adds Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) support to the sam-sql-database-tool plugin, expanding database compatibility beyond PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB.

### How was this change implemented?

- **pyproject.toml**: Added `pyodbc` dependency for MSSQL connectivity and `testcontainers[mssql]` for testing
- **database_service.py**: Added MSSQL-specific row count query using `sys.tables`/`sys.partitions` and extended string type detection to include `NVARCHAR`, `NCHAR`, `NTEXT`
- **conftest.py**: Added MSSQL test container configuration with `SqlServerContainer` and pyodbc connection URL
- **test_data.py**: Set `autoincrement=False` on all primary keys to allow explicit ID inserts (MSSQL IDENTITY column restriction)
- **test_sql_tool.py**: Cast rating to Float in aggregation test to handle MSSQL integer division behavior
- **test_config_features.py**: Added dialect-specific ALTER TABLE syntax (MSSQL omits `COLUMN` keyword in `ADD`)
- **README.md**: Updated documentation with MSSQL connection string example

### Key Design Decisions

- Chose `pyodbc` over `pymssql` as it's more widely supported and Microsoft-recommended, though it requires an ODBC Driver to be installed on the host system
- Used `autoincrement=False` in test tables rather than modifying INSERT statements to keep test queries database-agnostic

### How was this change tested?

- [x] Manual testing: Connected to local MSSQL Docker container and verified queries execute correctly
- [x] Unit tests: Existing unit tests pass
- [x] Integration tests: All integration tests pass across PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, and MSSQL (223 tests total)
- [x] Known limitations: Requires an ODBC Driver for SQL Server installed on the host system

### Is there anything the reviewers should focus on/be aware of?

- The MSSQL connection string requires `TrustServerCertificate=yes` for self-signed certificates (common in dev/test environments)
- Users will need to install the ODBC Driver separately - this is a system-level dependency that cannot be bundled with the Python package

author: copilot
body:
Supabase integration had blocking issues: signup created duplicate profiles, ad publishing failed on missing columns (`title_en`, `description_en`, `phone`), and RLS INSERT policy rejected new users due to timing issues.

## Schema Fixes

**Migration 034** adds missing columns with backwards compatibility:
- `title_en`, `description_en` to properties table (defaults copy from FR versions)
- `phone` column (both `phone` and `contact_phone` now set for compatibility)
- Helper function `can_insert_property()` to optimize RLS policy checks

## Authentication 

Removed manual profile upsert in `AuthContext.signUp()` - the database trigger `handle_new_user()` handles profile creation exclusively now. Eliminates race condition between auth user creation and profile availability.

```typescript
// Before: Double profile creation (trigger + manual)
const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signUp({...})
if (data?.user && !error) {
  await supabase.from('profiles').upsert([...]) // REMOVED
}

// After: Trigger handles it
const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signUp({...})
return { error: error || null }
```

## RLS Policy

Simplified properties INSERT policy to allow inserts when profile doesn't exist yet OR has correct role:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION can_insert_property(user_id UUID) RETURNS BOOLEAN AS $$
BEGIN
  RETURN user_id IS NOT NULL AND (
    NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = user_id) OR
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM profiles WHERE id = user_id 
            AND (user_role IN ('real_estate_advertiser', 'admin') OR is_admin = true))
  );
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE;
```

## Error Handling

Extracted error categorization into `getErrorMessage()` helper. Maps Postgres error codes to user-friendly messages (permission denied, validation, duplicates, missing fields) with technical details in dev mode only.

## Migration Required

Apply `supabase/migrations/034_fix_schema_mismatches.sql` before deployment.

## Documentation

Added comprehensive setup guides:
- `QUICK_SETUP.md` - 15-min setup walkthrough
- `TESTING_GUIDE.md` - Testing procedures with verification queries
- `MIGRATION_CHECKLIST.md` - Step-by-step migration with rollback procedures
- `AUDIT_REPORT.md` - Root cause analysis of all issues found

## Summary

- Add C++ implementation of `evtol_effectors_fmu_model` using the CPPFMU library for FMI 3.0 compliance
- Port Python model to native C++ for improved performance and reduced FMU size
- Update autopilot DAA scenario config to use the new C++ FMU

## Details

This PR introduces a pure C++ implementation of the eVTOL effectors FMU, replacing the Python-based version for scenarios where native performance is preferred.

### Features
- **6 tiltrotors** with pose outputs (position + quaternion orientation)
- **6 rotors** with spinning animation via quaternion rotation
- **Inputs:** `tilt_deg`, `proprotor_rpm`, `liftrotor_rpm`
- **Euler to quaternion conversion** matching scipy's `from_euler("zyx", [roll, pitch, yaw])` convention

### Build System
- CMake configuration using `FetchContent` to pull CPPFMU source directly from [PythonFMU3](https://github.com/stephensmith25/PythonFMU3) repository
- Cross-platform support (Linux, Windows, macOS)
- MSVC warning suppression for unimplemented optional FMI 3.0 features in third-party CPPFMU code
- Build scripts provided for both Linux/macOS (`.sh`) and Windows (`.bat`)

### Size Comparison
| Version | FMU Size |
|---------|----------|
| Python (`evtol_effectors_fmu_model.fmu`) | ~945 KB |
| C++ (`evtol_effectors_fmu_model_cpp.fmu`) | ~42 KB |

🚀 Release Notes — Authentication Flow Upgrade (MAUI .NET 10)
✅ Overview
This release introduces a fully modernized authentication flow for the MAUI application, aligned with .NET 10 lifecycle changes and best practices. It replaces deprecated APIs, stabilizes token handling, and ensures compatibility across Android, iOS, and Windows.

🔐 1. Authentication Startup Flow (CreateWindow Migration)
What changed
- Removed deprecated Application.MainPage usage.
- Implemented .NET 10‑compliant startup using CreateWindow().
- Added asynchronous initialization pipeline for auto‑login.
- Introduced a temporary loading screen during token validation.
Impact
- No more obsolete warnings.
- Startup is smoother and more reliable.
- App now supports future MAUI windowing changes.

🔑 2. Refresh Token Auto‑Login
What changed
- Added secure refresh token lookup via SecureStorage.
- Implemented AuthService.Refresh() call during startup.
- Automatically stores new access tokens when refresh succeeds.
- Falls back to login screen when refresh fails.
Impact
- Users stay logged in across app restarts.
- Reduced friction and improved UX.

🔒 3. SecureStorage Crash Fix
What changed
- Fixed ArgumentNullException caused by null token values.
- Added null guards before calling SecureStorage.SetAsync.
- Updated AuthResponse model to initialize strings safely.
Impact
- Eliminates Android JavaProxyThrowable crashes.
- Ensures token persistence is stable and predictable.

🧭 4. Navigation System Migration (No Shell)
What changed
- Removed all Shell.Current navigation and alerts.
- Implemented WindowHelper to access the active window.
- Updated ViewModels to use:
- WindowHelper.GetCurrentPage().Navigation.PushAsync(...)
- DisplayAlertAsync via the active window.
Impact
- Navigation now fully supports MVVM + NavigationPage.
- No more obsolete warnings from .NET 10.

🌐 5. HttpClient Modernization
What changed
- Fixed InvalidOperationException caused by missing BaseAddress.
- Added proper BaseAddress configuration in DI.
- Introduced DelegatingHandler pattern for attaching JWT tokens.
Impact
- All API calls now use correct absolute URLs.
- Token injection is clean, async‑safe, and production‑ready.

🧩 6. ViewModel Improvements
What changed
- Replaced [ObservableProperty] warnings with safe initialization.
- Ensured AOT compatibility for Android/Windows.
- Cleaned up login logic and error handling.
Impact
- ViewModels are stable, warning‑free, and ready for production.

📦 7. Pages + DI Integration
What changed
- Registered all pages and ViewModels in DI.
- Navigation now resolves pages via IServiceProvider.
Impact
- Cleaner architecture.
- Easier testing and future expansion.

🎉 Summary
This release delivers a fully modernized, stable, and .NET‑10‑compliant authentication system with:
- Safe token storage
- Auto‑login
- Clean navigation
- Crash‑free SecureStorage
- Proper HttpClient configuration
- MVVM‑friendly architecture
Your app is now ready for the next phase: feature pages, API integration, and role‑based UI.

## Summary
This PR fixes a type mismatch bug in the Subsonic API response structures where numeric fields were declared as Go's platform-dependent `int` type instead of the fixed-width `int32` type required by the Subsonic API XSD specification.

## Problem
On 64-bit systems, Go's `int` type is 64 bits wide, while the Subsonic API XSD schema specifies these fields as `xs:int`, which corresponds to a 32-bit signed integer. This inconsistency caused schema validation failures for strict API clients.

## Solution

author: ericch1
body:
Hi again Uncrustify team,

   As the continuation of #4587, this PR adds 6 new options to control line skipping in assignment alignment:

     - align_assign_span_num_{empty,pp,cmt}_lines
     - align_enum_equ_span_num_{empty,pp,cmt}_lines

   These new options let Uncrustify ignore (skip) a certain number of empty lines, preprocessor lines, or comment-only lines when it tries to align assignments and enum values, helping the alignment stay together and making the code look cleaner.

   By default, these new options are set to '0', so they don't change how things work unless you turn them on.

   **Example**

   When `align_assign_span = 1` and `align_assign_span_num_cmt_lines = 2` are active:

   Input:
```
     int var1 = 100;
     // comment line 1
     // comment line 2
     double var2 = 200;

     unsigned short var3 = 300;
```

   Output:

```
     int var1    = 100;
     // comment line 1
     // comment line 2
     double var2 = 200;

     unsigned short var3 = 300;
```

   The `=` of `var1` and `var2` are aligned because the 2 comment lines are skipped. But `var3` is not aligned because the empty line breaks the span.

   **Implementation details:**

   - Use GetNlCountFiltered() instead of GetNlCount() for newline handling (with an exception)
   - Maintain separate budget config for assign vs enum contexts
   - Reset budget after each alignment addition and when starting a new alignment group
   - Budget is context-aware: switches between assign and enum configs when recursing into enum braces

   **Tests:**

   - 14 new C tests covering all 6 options
   - 33 new C++ tests covering recursive contexts, mixed line types, and interleaved prototypes with defaults

   About this work: The first ideas came from the Claude Opus 4.5 AI. But I spent a lot of time checking, cleaning, fixing bugs, and making it much better before sharing it.

   I hope this helps! Please tell me if anything needs changes. Thank you!

ps: There are "holes" into tests numbers because I removed some duplicates after (having a hard time) debugging more complex cases which I added after the simpler ones and decided to remove the simpler ones.

|---|---|---|---|
| [github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/v2](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync) | `v2.5.1` → `v4.4.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/go/github.com%2fpuzpuzpuz%2fxsync%2fv2/v4.4.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/go/github.com%2fpuzpuzpuz%2fxsync%2fv2/v2.5.1/v4.4.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>puzpuzpuz/xsync (github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/v2)</summary>

### [`v4.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.3.0...v4.4.0)

- Micro-optimize `Map` for integer keys [#​185](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/185)
- Add `Map.RangeRelaxed` method for faster map iteration [#​187](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/187)
- Add `Map.DeleteMatching` method for batch entry deletion [#​186](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/186)

Read-heavy operations on `Map` with integer keys are now 24-29% faster due to a more efficient hash function, as well as a number of micro-optimizations.

`RangeRelaxed` is a much faster (\~11x), lock-free alternative to `Range`. The downside is that the same key may be visited by `RangeRelaxed` more than once if it is concurrently deleted and re-inserted during the iteration. `RangeRelaxed` should be preferred over `Range` in all cases when weaker consistency is acceptable.

```go
m := xsync.NewMap[string, int]()
m.Store("alice", 10)
m.Store("bob", 20)
m.Store("carol", 30)
m.Store("dave", 40)

// Iterate map entries and calculate sum of all values.
sum := 0
m.RangeRelaxed(func(key string, value int) bool {
	sum += value
	return true // continue iteration
})
```

`DeleteMatching` deletes all entries for which the delete return value of the input function is true. If the cancel return value is true, the iteration stops immediately. The function returns the number of deleted entries. The call locks a hash table bucket for the duration of evaluating the function for all entries in the bucket and performing deletions. It performs up to 20% faster than `Range` + `Delete`, yet if the percentage of the entries to-be-deleted is low, `RangeRelaxed` + `Delete` combination should be more efficient.

```go
// Delete entries with value greater than 25.
deleted := m.DeleteMatching(func(key string, value int) (delete, cancel bool) {
	return value > 25, false
})
```

### [`v4.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.2.0...v4.3.0)

- Add iterator function `Map.All` [#​181](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/181)
- Make shrink resize lock-free on target buckets [#​180](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/180)

`All` is similar to `Range`, but returns an `iter.Seq2`, so is compatible with Go 1.23+ iterators. All of the same caveats and behavior from `Range` apply to `All`.

```golang
m := xsync.NewMap[string, int]()
for i := range 100 {
  m.Store(strconv.Itoa(i), i)
}

// Will print all of the map entries
for key, val := range m.All() {
  fmt.Printf("m[%q] = %q\n")
}
```

Kudos to [@​llxisdsh](https://redirect.github.com/llxisdsh) and [@​moskyb](https://redirect.github.com/moskyb) for making this release happen.

### [`v4.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.1.0...v4.2.0)

- Cooperative parallel rehashing in `Map` [#​178](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/178)
- Use `runtime.cheaprand` instead of `fastrand` [#​177](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/177)

Introduces cooperative rehashing for `xsync.Map` this means that goroutines that execute write operations, such as `Compute` or `Store`, may participate in table rehashing when the hash table grows or shrinks. From now on, table rehashing never spawns additional goroutines.

This behavior is always enabled, so the `WithSerialResize` function is now marked as deprecated and acts as a no-op.

### [`v4.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v4.0.0...v4.1.0)

- New data structure: `UMPSCQueue` [#​168](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/168)
- Speed up `LoadAndDelete` and `Delete` in case of non-existing `Map` key [#​167](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/167)
- Parallel `Map` resize [#​170](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/issues/170)

`UMPSCQueue` is meant to serve as a replacement for a channel. However, crucially, it has infinite capacity. This is a very bad idea in many cases as it means that it never exhibits backpressure. In other words, if nothing is consuming elements from the queue, it will eventually consume all available memory and crash the process. However, there are also cases where this is desired behavior as it means the queue will dynamically allocate more memory to store temporary bursts, allowing producers to never block while the consumer catches up.

From now on, `Map` spawns additional goroutines to speed up resizing the hash table. This can be disabled when creating a `Map` with the new `WithSerialResize` setting:

```go
m := xsync.NewMap[int, int](xsync.WithSerialResize())
// resize will take place on the current goroutine only
for i := 0; i < 10000; i++ {
	m.Store(i, i)
}
```

Thanks [@​PapaCharlie](https://redirect.github.com/PapaCharlie) and [@​llxisdsh](https://redirect.github.com/llxisdsh) for the contributions!

### [`v4.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v4.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/compare/v3.5.1...v4.0.0)

- Minimal Golang version is now 1.24.
- All non-generic data structures are now removed. Generic versions should be used instead - they use the old names, but type aliases are present to simplify v3-to-v4 code migration.
- `MapOf`'s hasher API is gone. The default and only hash function is now based on `maphash.Comparable`.
- `Map`'s `Compute` API now supports no-op (cancel) compute operation.

Thanks [@​PapaCharlie](https://redirect.github.com/PapaCharlie) for making this release happen

##### Migration notes

- The old `*Of` types are kept as type aliases for the renamed data structures to simplify the migration, e.g. `MapOf` is an alias for `Map`.
- `NewMapOfPresized` function is gone. `NewMap` combined with `WithPresize` should be used instead.
- `Map.Compute` method now expects `valueFn` to return a `ComputeOp` value instead of a boolean flag. That's to support compute operation cancellation, so that the call does nothing.
- `Map.LoadOrTryCompute` method is renamed to `LoadOrCompute`. The old `LoadOrCompute` method is removed as it was redundant.

### [`v3.5.1`](https://redirect.github.com/puzpuzpuz/xsync/releases/tag/v3.5.1)

Update cube_build to use `prepare_output`.  

Some notes:
- I moved a datamodels.open call out of the DataTypes class, so it now expects open datamodels and does not attempt to close anything.  
- I moved a reference to the input datamodels out of `self.input_models` for the class, to make sure they can be garbage collected, even if the step is still in scope.  
- I removed an unnecessary datamodel copy in IFUCubeData.build_ifucube.
- I raised an error in a couple places where the step was warning and returning None.  The calling code in the pipelines does not check for None in the return value, so these conditions would have resulted in crashes anyway.

**Changes:**

2.  **`app/main.py`**: Added `get_api_key` dependency using `fastapi.security.APIKeyHeader` and `secrets.compare_digest`. Applied it to the `FastAPI` app to protect all routes.
3.  **`tests/test_api.py`**: Updated tests to include the `X-API-Key` header and added a test for unauthorized access.
4.  **`app/__init__.py`**: Created to resolve import issues during testing.
5.  **`.jules/sentinel.md`**: Added journal entry for the vulnerability.

**Impact:**
All requests to the backend API now require a valid `X-API-Key` header. This prevents unauthorized access to file operations. This is a breaking change for any clients currently using the API without authentication.

author: pythonpedro99
body:
### Motivation
- Introduce a two-phase conditioning scheme so the dynamics predictor can be conditioned first on continuous latent actions and then gradually on VQ-quantized actions while the VQ commitment weight is ramped in sync.
- Keep changes minimal and localized to the forward conditioning path and commitment scheduling so existing training, dataloading, optimizers, EMA updates, and logging are unaffected.

### Description
- Add a small schedule helper `two_phase_schedule(global_step, warmup_steps, mix_steps, target_commit)` in `train.py` that returns `alpha` and `lambda_commit` with safe handling of `mix_steps==0` and clamping to [0,1].
- Wire the schedule into the training loop (`train.py`) to compute `alpha` and `lambda_commit` when `cfg.two_phase.enabled` is true, set `model.vq_model.commitment = lambda_commit` and expose `model.two_phase_enabled` / `model.two_phase_alpha` for the model to consume.
- Blend continuous and VQ actions in the conditioning path inside `models/visual_world_model.py` by replacing `act_base = quantized_latent_actions` with `act_base = (1-alpha)*latent_actions + alpha*quantized_latent_actions` when two-phase is active, preserving the existing tiled/concatenation behavior and asserting unchanged behavior when disabled.
- Add `two_phase` defaults to `conf/train.yaml` (`enabled: false`, `warmup_steps: 0`, `mix_steps: 0`) and reuse the existing `model.commitment` value as the ramp target.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.
- The change is limited to the conditioning path and commitment scalar and was committed after local edits; behavior should remain identical when `two_phase.enabled=false` and deterministic given the same seed and `global_step` schedule.

author: wifitldev
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a minimal self-contained OS repository that boots from BIOS (MBR → stage2) into a custom x86_64 kernel and exposes a tiny userspace-like environment (shell + GUI explorer) without external kernel/SDK dependencies.
- Supply a reproducible host-side toolchain and disk image generation so `make` produces a raw disk image bootable in QEMU.

### Description
- Add a two-stage BIOS bootloader: `boot/stage1.asm` (MBR) and `boot/stage2.asm` (loads stages, enables A20, gathers e820, sets up VBE, switches to long mode and jumps to kernel at `0x00100000`).
- Implement a freestanding x86_64 kernel under `kernel/` with entry glue (`arch/x86_64/entry.asm`), IDT/ISRs (`arch/x86_64/idt.h`, `arch/x86_64/isr.asm`), interrupt handling (`kernel/interrupts.c`), context switch (`arch/x86_64/context.asm`), and a small kernel main in `kernel/kernel.c` that initializes subsystems.
- Provide core subsystems and drivers: console VGA text, minimal libc (`kernel/lib/*`), GDT/IDT, PIT timer, PS/2 keyboard/mouse, ATA PIO reader, physical memory manager (bitmap), simple heap (`kmalloc` bump allocator), trivial paging stub, round-robin task scheduler and context switching (`kernel/task.*`), and syscall stubs (`kernel/syscall.c`/`kernel/sys/syscall.h`).
- Implement a simple on-disk filesystem format OSFS and host `tools/mkfs.c` that builds `fs.img` from `fsroot/`; kernel mounts it via `kernel/fs/*` and exposes a tiny VFS layer `kernel/fs/vfs.*` used by shell and explorer.
- Add GUI framebuffer primitives and a minimal Explorer task (`kernel/gui/*`) plus a shell task (`kernel/shell/*`) with basic commands; include `Makefile` targets to build everything and assemble `disk.img` and `run` target to start QEMU.
- Fixes and build adjustments made during rollout include corrections to inline asm in `mm/paging.c`, stage2 sizing/fields, keyboard ISR split, timer tick wiring, and build list updates so the kernel links cleanly.

### Testing
- Built kernel with `make -C /workspace/trashbin kernel` which completed successfully and produced `build/kernel/kernel.bin` (link/objcopy step passed). (succeeded)
- Generated the filesystem and full disk image with `make -C /workspace/trashbin disk.img` which produced `fs.img` and `disk.img` and completed without errors; `qemu` run target is provided via `make run`. (succeeded)

author: ivanpleshkov
body:
There is a mechanism for locking collection updates, which is obsolete.

There is a `Collection::updates_lock` with `RwLock` type. By design, all update operations are protected by `read` of this mutex. There is a function `lock_updates` with `write`-lock. But this function is unused.

It means that the mutex `Collection::updates_lock` protects nothing right now, and it's safe to delete it. It's not under-progress feature because this mutex is pretty old.

body:
Addresses Git ref locking failures that occur when local tracking refs become corrupted or out of sync with remote. Error manifests as:

```
Error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/FEATURE/portabilidade-nova': 
is at 359489fce51380db13abdcfbe7b3733fd555dde8 but expected bb271a5ed9f77b4ffc4257d281c31ef8b0c7b1f0
```

## Changes

- **GIT_REF_LOCKING_ISSUE.md**: Troubleshooting guide covering root causes (force-pushed branches, corrupted refs, network interruptions), progressive fix methods, and prevention
- **fix-git-refs.sh** / **fix-git-refs.ps1**: Cross-platform automation scripts that:
  - Detect corrupted refs from fetch errors
  - Apply progressive fix strategies (prune → specific ref cleanup → full ref rebuild)
  - Stash/restore uncommitted changes
  - Verify repository health post-fix
- **README.md**: Project documentation with quick-start and troubleshooting sections
- **Api/README.md**: Reference to troubleshooting guide

## Implementation Details

Scripts use secure temp file handling (`mktemp` vs `/tmp`) and POSIX-compliant regex (`sed` vs `grep -P`) for portability. Ref extraction handles both single and double quote patterns in Git error messages.

Example automated fix flow:
```bash
./fix-git-refs.sh
# Detects: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/FEATURE/branch'
# Applies: git update-ref -d refs/remotes/origin/FEATURE/branch
# Rebuilds: git fetch origin
# Verifies: git fsck
```

### Motivation
- Prevent the screen from sleeping while the app is in fullscreen, but avoid holding a Wake Lock when the app is not fullscreen to conserve resources.
- Provide a graceful fallback when the Wake Lock API is unavailable or when requests fail.

### Description
- Added a `wakeLock` variable and two helpers: `requestWakeLock()` to request `navigator.wakeLock.request('screen')` and `releaseWakeLock()` to release it and clear the reference.
- Hooked Wake Lock behavior into the `fullscreenchange` event so `requestWakeLock()` runs when `document.fullscreenElement` is present and `releaseWakeLock()` runs on exit.
- Added error handling and a `release` event listener to keep `wakeLock` state consistent and silently tolerate browsers that lack the Wake Lock API.

author: strombetta
body:
### Motivation
- Address reported ShellCheck syntax errors (SC1009, SC1046, SC1047, SC1072) caused by unbalanced `if`/`fi` blocks in `scripts/check-toolchain.sh` so static analysis and CI can pass.
- Ensure `make check` reliably validates the final toolchain by building the `toolchain` target before running checks.
- Make the check output ordering and diagnostics predictable by grouping related validations (binutils, linux-headers, gcc, musl, sysroot).

### Description
- Update `Makefile` so the `check` target depends on `toolchain` by changing the rule to `check: guard-TARGET toolchain` to ensure the final GCC and toolchain binaries exist before validation.
- Refactor `scripts/check-toolchain.sh` into explicit, self-contained functions: `check_binutils`, `check_linux_headers`, `check_gcc`, `check_musl`, and `check_sysroot`, and add the `check_step` helper for consistent output.
- Preserve and centralize existing logic: use `resolve_tool()` to search `$PREFIX/bin` and `$TOOLCHAIN_TARGET_DIR/bin`, verify `gcc --print-sysroot` and `gcc -dumpmachine`, detect musl loader and libc artifacts, and validate ELF `Machine:` via `readelf` against `EXPECTED_MACHINE`.
- Replace the ad-hoc inline checks with an ordered call sequence at the end of the script: `check_binutils`, `check_linux_headers`, `check_gcc`, `check_musl`, `check_sysroot`, thereby closing all `if`/`fi` blocks and eliminating the ShellCheck errors.

### Testing

author: pondsec
body:
### Motivation
- Ein umfassendes, professionelles Rollen- und Rechte-System soll ermöglichen, dass z.B. Kunden nur eigene Tickets sehen/erstellen und nichts bearbeiten oder Inventar ändern dürfen, während Admins volle Rechte haben und individuellen Rollen spezifische Rechte zugewiesen werden können.
- Standardrollen (Admin, Mitarbeiter, Kunde) sowie die Möglichkeit, eigene Rollen mit granularen Berechtigungen zu erstellen und Benutzern zuzuweisen, sind erforderlich, um feingranulare Zugangskontrolle bereitzustellen.

### Description
- Neue Datenbank-Elemente und Seeder: hinzugefügt wurden Tabellen `roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`, `user_roles` sowie `seed_permissions`/`seed_roles`/`ensure_default_roles` und Vordefinitionen in `PERMISSIONS`/`DEFAULT_ROLES` mit Standardrechten und -rollen; während der DB-Initialisierung werden Rollen/Berechtigungen erzeugt und die Standardrolle zugewiesen.
- Backend-RBAC-Logik: hinzugefügt `get_user_access`, `user_can`, `require_permission(s)`-Dekoratoren und Ticket-Eigentümer-Logik (`ensure_ticket_access`) sowie automatische Zuweisung der Standardrolle bei Benutzererstellung und AD-Import.
- Endpunkte: neue Endpunkte und Erweiterungen für Rollen/Permissions/Benutzerrollen (`/api/roles`, `/api/permissions`, `/api/users/<id>/roles`, `/api/me`) und Berechtigungsprüfungen an vielen bestehenden APIs (Kategorien, Geräte, Assets, Tickets, Alerts, Notifications, AD, Maintenance, Activity, Stats etc.).
- UI: Templates und JS aktualisiert, um Navigation, Aktionen und Modals anhand der Berechtigungen zu zeigen/verbergen (`templates/*.html`, `static/tickets.js`); Benutzerverwaltung enthält Rollenübersicht, Rolle erstellen/bearbeiten, Rollenzuweisung per Modal; clientseitig werden `window.inventoryPermissions`/`window.inventoryIsSuperuser` gesetzt und in Alpine-Apps genutzt.

### Testing
- Abhängigkeiten installiert via `pip install -r requirements.txt` und Installation der benötigten Pakete (inkl. `ldap3`) war erfolgreich. (erfolgreich)
- Entwicklungsserver gestartet mit `python app.py`; Datenbank wurde initialisiert, Default-Admin erstellt und Rollen/Berechtigungen wurden beim Start eingesät. (erfolgreich)
- Versuchte automatisierte UI-Prüfung mit Playwright schlug fehl aufgrund eines Chromium- / Headless-Browsercrashs (SIGSEGV) in der Laufzeitumgebung, das nicht den neuen Code betrifft, aber das automatische Screenshot/Selenium-Laufwerk verhindert hat. (fehlgeschlagen)
- Ergebnis: API- und DB-Änderungen wurden durch Start und Initialisierung validiert; browserbasierte End-to-end-Screenshot-Prüfung konnte wegen der Container-Browser-Instabilität nicht abgeschlossen werden.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
💡 **What:**
Replaced the inefficient in-memory aggregation of top services in `adminController.ts` with a database-level `GROUP BY` query using Prisma.

🎯 **Why:**
The previous implementation fetched *all* bookings for the last month into memory to count service usage. This is resource-heavy (O(N) memory and data transfer). The database aggregation is much faster and reduces application memory usage.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
A benchmark with 10,000 bookings showed a **31x performance improvement**:
- **Before:** ~527 ms
- **After:** ~16 ms

🛠️ **Other Changes:**
- Fixed a `const` reassignment bug in `bookingController.ts` that prevented the project from compiling.
- Added `backend/benchmark.ts` to reproduce the performance test (requires SQLite environment or configured Postgres).

### Motivation
- Allow an entrypoint-initialized logger to be updated or replaced by downstream workflow code so workflows can emit their own log files and logging configuration without being blocked by a prior initialization.

author: rneswold
body:
These API improvements were the recommendation of ChatGPT in GitHub's Copilot feature. Some of the code it flagged was stuff I wrote earlier when I was less experienced with Rust. They were very good changes. Although ChatGPT showed examples of how the improvements would look and be used, I wrote all the changes required in the `drmem-api` and driver crates.

The first change converted a boxed closure into an enumerated type which required no allocating.

The second was to use `async` methods in the driver crate instead of specifying complicated, boxed, pinned futures with specialty traits.

Next, functions and methods that needed any path of a device name were requiring the caller to create the correct type. Now we've defined an Into<> trait so callers can pass `&str` and the functions will convert it internally. This really cleaned up some code.

Finally, instead of hand-writing code to verify and access the driver config parameters, we now use `serde`. A driver can describe their parameters in a struct and `serde` will do the validation. This is a huge usability win for authors of device drivers.

Creates a comprehensive skills library for AI coding agents working with NEAR Protocol, following the vercel-labs/agent-skills format.

## Skills Added

### `near-smart-contracts` - Rust Smart Contract Development
5 rules covering:
- Security patterns (storage validation, access control, reentrancy)
- Contract structure (`#[near_bindgen]`, initialization, collections)
- Cross-contract calls (promise chaining, callback handling)
- Testing (workspaces-rs integration tests)

### `near-dapps` - Frontend Development
3 rules covering:
- Wallet integration (@near-wallet-selector multi-wallet setup)
- Contract interaction (view methods via RPC, change methods with transactions)
- Transaction handling (gas allocation, error handling, receipt verification)

### `near-ai` - AI Agent Development
2 rules covering:
- NEAR AI inference endpoints (model selection, streaming, function calling)
- Agent architecture (modular design, tool composition, registry integration)

### `near-intents` - Cross-chain Swaps
Vendored from SurgeCode/near-intents-skill. 15 rules covering 1Click API integration, chain-specific deposits (EVM/Solana/TON/etc), React patterns.

Individual rules provide ❌ Incorrect / ✅ Correct code examples with explanations.

author: brln-devlabs
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent leaked POSIX shared memory segments created for plotting by ensuring creators unlink them on shutdown to avoid resource-tracker errors and leftover segments.
- Avoid multiprocessing resource-tracker conflicts by preferring the `spawn` start method for worker processes.

### Description
- Added `import multiprocessing` and a `_configure_multiprocessing()` helper that calls `multiprocessing.set_start_method("spawn")` when possible and invoked it from `main()`.
- Introduced a `_SHM_REGISTRY` set and updated `_create_shared_memory()` to record created shared memory names in the registry.
- Added `_cleanup_shared_memory()` which unlinks and closes any shared memory segments tracked in `_SHM_REGISTRY` and cleared the registry.
- Call `
_cleanup_shared_memory()` from `TransceiverUI.on_close()` to ensure cleanup on application shutdown.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.
